Valid XML documents differ in bytes while parsing identically — measured on the real `registry.xml`: single-quoting one attribute and spacing one `=` gives 12,985 bytes against 12,983, `diff` exits 1, and the parsed trees are **identical**. Byte instruments are right for "this bundle modified nothing" and for a golden-output promise; they are the wrong instrument for "the content is unchanged".
Owner: no bundle. The archived instance is immutable and closed; this entry exists so the rule is written down where the next author will find it.
**Method note against the authority.** Two errors in one review, both of the kind this record keeps recording. "Every prior bundle used the base-commit form" was a population claim made from the specs the authority happened to have read — the measurement above says 16 of 17. And the byte figures first reported (12,939 → 12,945) were JavaScript string `.length`, which counts UTF-16 code units, not bytes; `wc -c` gives 12,983. Reporting code units as bytes inside an argument about choosing the instrument that answers the question is the error the argument was about.

Finding.Title: ### F233 — `C-ROOT-WINDOW` pays `F226` without delivering its remedy: pre-payment as a headroom device puts a false `PaidBy` on the record, and the ratification it rode on never mentioned the semantics. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
The row: `registry-retired.xml:275`, `<Pays>F216 F182 F193 F190 F225 F226</Pays>`. The reason the spec gives for the last two tokens is headroom and nothing else — *"The pre-payment is what makes the next flush possible at all; that is why the row names both staged tokens"* (`.ngrace/changes/archive/C-ROOT-WINDOW/spec.xml:144`-147), carried verbatim through `-2` and `-3` and ratified three times. What [F226](#f226) describes is the teaching surface: eighteen measured gaps in `skills/ngrace/*`, owner "a chartered bundle on the teaching surface". **Measured 2026-09-11 at `ed67f45`:** `git diff --stat 8bfa3b7..ed67f45 -- skills/ plugins/` is empty — PR #86 and PR #87 between them changed no skill file. So the code `F226` describes still matches its description, and D28.1's findings rule has exactly that semantic half — a finding retires when *"the code it describes no longer matches"* (`C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2/spec.xml:333`); `PaidBy` naming an archived bundle is the machine-checkable proxy for it, not a substitute. The moment `F226` flushes it is eligible, moves with `PaidBy` `C-ROOT-WINDOW`, and `derivePayerMap` is first-row-wins (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:415`, `:425`), so no later row — including the one that actually delivers the remedy — can ever claim the token. `F225` is the milder neighbour: its remedy shipped in PR #86 (`C-FLUSH-AND-REPAIR`, a row-less bundle that "pays nothing and retires nothing", its spec `:39`), so the attribution is wrong but the semantic half holds.
**Whose error.** The authority's: it wrote the pre-payment into three specs, argued only the window, and put the row to the maintainer for ratification on that argument — the D28.1 half was never in front of him. The same session's handoff then listed "the skills bundle (`F226`)" as queued work beside "`F225`/`F226` are pre-paid", and did not notice that the two lines contradict. **The rule this settles:** a `Pays` token names a finding whose described defect the bundle delivers; minting a token to relieve a ceiling is not a payment, and a ceiling that blocks a flush is paid by a remedy or by the two-wave sequencing the flush precedent already allows, never by a proxy row.
**Disposition, decided 2026-09-11 with the maintainer** (variant chosen over renumbering the skills finding, which would leave every archived citation of `F226` dangling, and over accepting the attribute): `F226` flushes as-is and retires under the false `PaidBy`; this entry is the record's correction beside it; the teaching-surface bundle cites retired `F226` as its charter and pays `F233` by delivering `F226`'s remedy. The enforcement half — whether a validator can check the semantic rule at all, or only refuse `Pays` tokens absent from the record at the mint — belongs with [F197](#f197) and [F198](#f198), the payment-integrity bundle.
Owner: the chartered bundle on the teaching surface, which pays this entry by delivering `F226`'s remedy. Neighbour to [F226](#f226), [F197](#f197) (payments minted from prose) and [F198](#f198) (a settled finding with no row to pay it — the inverse defect).

Finding.Title: ### F234 — the teaching gaps measured after `F226`: five more in the authoring skills, and the reviewer skill teaches none of the checks the authority's own failures were about. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-11 at `3f8a5ca`**, by three executor dispatches' `SKILL GAPS` fields on `C-FLUSH-AND-UNPIN` (spec, plan, implementation) and by the authority reading `ngrace-reviewer/SKILL.md` whole; every absence searched with a pattern wider than the claim across all four skill trees, zero hits each. Skills unchanged since [F226](#f226)'s measurement (`git log 8bfa3b7..3f8a5ca -- skills/ngrace/`: no commits), so its eighteen stand as written; the five below are new, and the six reported this session that restate items 11, 13, 16 and 17 are not counted twice.
**Authoring skills, new.** (19) `ngrace-spec` `shape_sources` names `ngrace spec new` as the primary write path with no carve-out for the case where the skeleton is wrong for the artifact — a rich, precedent-shaped spec is rewritten wholesale; the executor learned the answer from the archive, not the skill. (20) `ngrace-plan` `command_phase_rules` never states the stage rule: a recorded task `Verification` command exits 0 at the stage that task runs, and a target-mode lint's pre-approval exit 1 is not a defect (`F184`'s refinement). (21) `ngrace-execute`'s `attempt` kind teaches the red-first ordering but not that the red run's output is report evidence to paste — a hand-written "it failed" is the same non-evidence as a hand-written "it passed".
**Reviewer skill, the larger half.** `ngrace-reviewer`'s checklist is structural — artifacts present, indexes route, statuses valid, scopes explicit — and its `mechanized_first` block runs `ngrace review` at three moments. It teaches nothing of the checks whose absence this record has paid for on the reviewer's own side: (22) read the artifact whole before a verdict, not the brief's conformance (`D27`; [F136.1](#f136.1)); (23) an implementer's report is a claim — drive the product on a copy before accepting it (this session: a plan approved on a read and a review run, re-driven only after the maintainer asked *"do you empirically check reports?"*); (24) derive the forced-file set from the Goals, not from the write-scope Constraint's own list ([F227](#f227)); (25) every criterion is probed in both directions on a throwaway copy before it is approved — the reviewer's half of `F226` item 10; (26) the full CI runs in a faithful copy of the post-close state, carrying the plan at `applied`, not only the `CloseEvidence` commands ([F231](#f231); the copy without the plan reds on `change.applied-plan-missing`, measured this session); (27) an assertion or probe is checked against the state the artifact's own life cycle produces next, never only the state at approval ([F225](#f225), [F229](#f229), [F232](#f232) — three instances, the third approved by a reviewer who had the rule in hand).
**One more, measured by the executor that authored the repair's own spec (28).** `ngrace-spec` `acceptance_criteria_anchors` teaches that a forgotten `AC-*` "still warn[s] unmapped" without its firing precondition: the warning is produced only against an active `plan.xml`; a draft spec whose only unmapped non-`CloseEvidence` criterion is the one the plan will map lints 0/0 with no plan present (measured 2026-09-11 at `3f8a5ca`). An author who reads the sentence expects a warning the tool cannot yet give, and takes silence for a mapped criterion. Adjacent to `F226` item 4, not a restatement of it.
**And one from the revision of that same spec (29).** `ngrace-spec` teaches create → review → gate and never says what a *draft* is: that an unapproved `spec.xml` is revised in place, and only an approved artifact is immutable and repaired by supersede. The executor revising a draft had to be told by the brief that `D27` binds approved artifacts only; `ngrace-plan` carries the equivalent sentence for plans (`approved_plan_immutability`) and `ngrace-spec` carries none.
**Universality, re-measured.** Zero occurrences of `RM-GOVERNED-PATH`, any record file name, or any `F`-token in the four skill trees at `3f8a5ca`; the rule for the repair is unchanged: the skill states the rule generically, the record keeps the provenance. `check-teaching-surface.ts` is the instrument that asserts skill text, and its refusal is still silent ([F199](#f199)).
Owner: the chartered bundle on the teaching surface, with [F226](#f226)'s eighteen — one bundle, four skills and their packaged mirror, paying this entry, [F233](#f233), and the live findings whose remedy is the rule the skill lacks. Neighbour to [F226](#f226) and [F231](#f231).

Finding.Title: ### F224 — the lifecycle's two most consequential transitions are hand-edits, and the tool ships a lint rule for the half-done state instead of a verb that cannot half-do it. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
`ngrace gate approve` writes `draft` to `approved` and fingerprints those bytes. `ngrace supersede` writes `superseded` onto spec **and** plan and renames the bundle directory, rolling both writes back on failure (`src/gates/ledger.ts:1449`-1470). Between them sits the transition neither owns: nothing in the CLI writes `applied`, and nothing moves an applied bundle to `archive/`.
**Measured 2026-09-10 at `8bfa3b7`.** The complete verb surface is `context cursor doctor file gate graph lint module plan review scaffold spec status supersede verification` (`ngrace --help`). Every occurrence of the token `applied` in non-test source under `src/` and `scripts/` is a **read** — the status checks in `lint/core.ts`, `review/core.ts`, `grace-status.ts`, `artifact/scope.ts`, `artifact/grammar.ts`, `gates/ledger.ts:468` — and not one is a write. `gate` states the refusal in its own usage text: *"Does not set status=applied and does not move bundles (invariant 8)"* (`src/gates/command.ts:492`). The shipped procedure prescribes the hand-edit: `skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md:42` — *"The gate does not itself author `status` or archive paths"* — and `:43` — *"Only after both gates permit, set spec and plan to `applied` and archive the complete bundle."*
**What the hand-edit costs, item by item.** No fingerprint is taken of the applied bytes, so the one state the record treats as final is the only one never bound to its content. No `Decision` records that the write happened, so `run-ledger.xml` shows the gates permitting and nothing performing. No instrument checks that the write landed on the root element. And the status write and the directory move are separate acts with nothing joining them, so an interruption between them leaves a bundle applied in `active/` or archived while still `approved`.
**The tool already expects this to go wrong.** `src/lint/core.ts:161` ships `change.applied-plan-missing` — *"An applied archived bundle requires an applied plan.xml"* — a diagnostic whose only cause is a hand-edit that reached the spec and stopped. A verb writing both artifacts in one call cannot produce that state at all.
**Driven this session, the near-miss that makes it concrete.** In `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3`'s plan the token `status="applied"` occurs **three** times: once as the root attribute and twice inside prose describing the close ceremony. A substitution over the file corrupts two sentences instead of transitioning the artifact. The close survived only because the edit was pinned to line 1 and then verified by position — which is a human doing an instrument's job, and the same category error as [F216](#f216), where the record's root attributes are hand-maintained on every write and the only tool that rewrites them refuses to run unless something moves.
**What this overturns, named.** Not `invariant 8`: its requirement is that a state-changing write needs an explicit trigger rather than an implicit one, and `gate approve` already writes status and fingerprints under that same invariant. A dedicated verb *is* an explicit trigger; what the invariant forbids is `gate apply` mutating as a side effect of evaluating a gate, and a separate verb preserves that separation exactly. What it does overturn is the procedural sentence in `ngrace-execute` (`:42`-43) that assigns the write to the operator, and that sentence has no recorded argument behind it — searched at this commit: `invariant 8` appears in `src/grace-cursor.ts:863`, `src/gates/command.ts:492` and the `RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY` plan, and states only the explicit-trigger requirement.
Owner: a chartered bundle, governed by [D37](#d37), which rules that status transitions belong to `ngrace` because that is where the sanctioned path is instrumented — `ngrace apply --change C-*`, writing `applied` to spec and plan after the apply gate permits, fingerprinting those bytes and recording the write in `run-ledger.xml`; and the archive move performed with `supersede`'s existing write-then-rename-with-rollback shape rather than by hand. Neighbour to [F216](#f216) (hand-maintained XML metadata with no owning verb) and [F214](#f214) (the ledger records that a command ran, never who ran it).

Finding.Title: ### F236 — `ngrace-plan` has no baseline-polarity doctrine: nothing says a `BaselineAssertions` needle may not assert what the bundle changes, and the plan that repairs the skills shipped twenty-eight such needles. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-11 at `5507107`.** The first draft of `C-TAUGHT-RULES/plan.xml` carried 22 `MustContain` and 6 `MustNotContain` content needles in `BaselineAssertions`, at least eight of which the bundle flips by design (`F9.8` must-contain in both `ngrace-execute` trees; `checkTaughtRules` must-not-contain in the runner). Driven by the authority on a faithful copy with the plan at `approved`: current-mode root lint exits 1 with three `assertion.MustContain`/`MustNotContain` errors — *"Baseline assertion failures: 3. Current mode cannot tell whether writes have started"* — the [F211](#f211) mechanism, which would have reddened every task boundary from the first write to the close. The executor's own boundary drives had run with the plan at `draft`, which current mode does not evaluate ([F231](#f231)'s lesson: drive the state that will exist). The revision restored the precedent's form — `MustExist`, `MustVerify`, `MustPassCommand` — and the same probe exits 0.
**The gap.** `ngrace-plan` `must_do` row 4 demands "non-empty machine-checkable baseline and target assertions" and says nothing about polarity or stability: the rule that a baseline asserts only what the bundle leaves unchanged — and that token red-first belongs in tests and probes, not in baseline needles — is nowhere in the skill. A second half, from the same revision: row 15's "do not add those paths to ObservedWriteScope" states the rule without its ground (`src/review/core.ts:1037` `isReviewedChangeSpecOrPlanPath`, `:1013`-1025 `isCliLifecyclePath` — the entries are structurally redundant, not merely disfavored), and the executor listed them on an older precedent's example.
**A third, from the first dispatch under the taught skills (2026-09-12).** `ngrace-spec` `shape_sources` names `references/change-spec-template.xml` without saying what the path is relative to; a cold executor resolved it from the repository root, found nothing, and reported the teaching source as missing. It exists at `skills/ngrace/ngrace-spec/references/` — the skill's own directory. One clause ("relative to this skill's directory") closes it.
**A fourth, from the first plan authored under the taught skills (2026-09-12).** `ngrace-plan` `must_do` 19 ("drive every planned command on a prototype before the plan is approved") reads as the tasks' `Verification` commands; that the spec's `CloseEvidence` commands and the full CI are driven in a faithful post-close copy at plan time is taught in `ngrace-spec` (item 10) and `ngrace-reviewer` (item 26) but not where the plan author reads — one clause on row 19 closes it.
**Why this is not in `C-TAUGHT-RULES`.** Its spec was approved at `5507107` enumerating twenty-nine rules; absorbing a thirtieth requires a supersede ([D27](#d27)), and a supersede for one doctrine sentence costs more than the sentence — the conflict `D11` requires for a deferral, stated as such.
Owner: the next teaching-surface increment, chartered after `C-TAUGHT-RULES` closes, paying this entry with the baseline-polarity rule in `ngrace-plan` `must_do` and the exclusion's ground beside row 15. Neighbour to [F211](#f211), [F226](#f226) and [F234](#f234).

Finding.Title: ### F237 — two red-direction fixtures mutated `registry.xml` by name, so the moment the close moved the row they mutated nothing and their `toThrow` failed: `F229`'s class on the red side, found by the close's own `CloseEvidence` run. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-12 at the `C-TAUGHT-RULES` close**, after `--retire` had moved the row and four findings. `bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` — the `CloseEvidence` command of `AC-ROW-PAYS` and `AC-RECORD-VALID`, run from the archived spec's bytes — exited 1: 85 pass / 2 fail, *"red direction — a Pays token outside the six reddens the exact-set clause"* and *"red direction — a StatusText naming a token outside Pays reddens the row's prose law"*, both `expect(received).toThrow(expected)`. The fixture helper `plantedTaughtRegistry(mutateLive)` applied its mutation to `registry.xml` only; post-close the row sits in `registry-retired.xml`, so the `String.replace` found nothing, the copy was unmutated, the walk stayed green, and the red direction proved nothing. The green production tests were correct at both states; only the reds were pinned to the live layer — the mirror image of [F229](#f229), whose fixture was *planted* into the live layer. Repaired at the close by the authority (disclosed in the close commit): the helper now mutates whichever layer holds the row; 87 pass / 0 fail post-close.
**Who missed it, in order.** The executor's plan-time drive ran the suite post-close at 82 tests — the two reds did not yet exist; they were written at T-005 and driven pre-close only. The authority's pre-close verification ran the suite at 87 on the pre-close tree and drove the checker's reds on a copy, but never drove the *suite's own red fixtures* through the close — [F231](#f231)'s rule ("drive the state the life cycle produces next") applied to green assertions and not to red fixtures, which are assertions too.
**The rule, sharpened.** A red-direction fixture is a state-dependent artifact exactly as a green assertion is: it must locate its target by walking both layers and mutate the holder it finds, never a file named in advance; and the pre-close review drives the suite in the post-close copy, including its reds, before approving the plan that adds them. `ngrace-reviewer`'s new `review_judgment` block says "check an assertion or probe against the state the artifact's own life cycle produces next" — this entry is the first measurement that the sentence needs to say *fixture* too.
Owner: the next teaching-surface increment (with [F236](#f236)), which sharpens the reviewer sentence and adds the fixture rule beside `ngrace-plan`'s probe row. Neighbour to [F229](#f229), [F231](#f231) and [F236](#f236).

Finding.Title: ### F238 — two "payment absence" tests pin their bundle's staged tokens *unpaid* in the production payer map, so the first bundle that pays any of them reds the suite: `F225`'s class in the payer-map dimension, shipped twice and approved twice. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-12 at the `C-FLUSH-TWO-WAVES` verification.** `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` carried, from PR #86, *"C-FLUSH-AND-REPAIR payment absence"* asserting that the production `derivePayerMap` mints none of `F221 F222 F223 F224 D37`, and the delivered wave-2 suite added *"C-FLUSH-TWO-WAVES payment absence"* asserting the same of `F230 F235 F236 F237 D38` — `toBeUndefined()` per token, unconditionally. Each is true at its bundle's close and false at the first legitimate payment of any named token: the guard bundle pays `F222` and `F223`, the verb bundle pays `F224`, and the suite would red on the payment it exists to record. Driven: a planted archived row paying `F222 F235` on a copy moved three elements and reddened both tests as written.
**The class.** [F225](#f225) pinned findings `live`; [F229](#f229) planted a fixture into the live layer; [F232](#f232) pinned two tokens absent from the findings files; [F237](#f237) pinned a red fixture to the live layer; this pins tokens absent from the *payer map*. Five instances, one rule — an assertion describes the state the record's own life cycle leaves next, never the state at approval — and the `C-FLUSH-AND-REPAIR` instance was written by the very bundle that repaired `F225` and approved by the reviewer holding that rule.
**The payment-invariant form**, applied to both at the `C-FLUSH-TWO-WAVES` close (disclosed in its close commit): "this bundle pays nothing" is asserted as no `Row` in either registry layer carrying the bundle's name and no payer-map entry naming it as payer — true at the close and true after any other bundle pays those tokens. The discriminating direction (an isolated root with a planted row mints its tokens) is unchanged.
**Why the reviewer missed it twice.** The reviewer's check for this class asks whether an assertion survives the *bundle's own* close; both tests do. The state that breaks them is a *later* bundle's payment — the rule in `ngrace-reviewer`'s `review_judgment` says "the state the artifact's own life cycle produces next", and the record's life cycle is not one bundle's. The sentence needs "any later lawful move of the record", not "the artifact's".
Owner: the next teaching-surface increment (with [F236](#f236) and [F237](#f237)) for the reviewer sentence; the repair itself is delivered. Neighbour to [F225](#f225), [F232](#f232) and [F237](#f237).

Finding.Title: ### F239 — three authoring skills teach "argv token `explain`" as the way to explain a shape or code, and the binary has no `explain` verb: the token is a flag on `lint`, and the skill never says so. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-12 at `a1d5829`, from the executor's `SKILL GAPS` on the `C-APPLY-VERB` spec dispatch, re-driven by the authority.** `grep -rn 'argv token \`explain\`' skills/ngrace plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace` → **12 lines** across both trees: `ngrace-spec/SKILL.md:17` and `ngrace-plan/SKILL.md:11` ("Explain a shape or code: argv token `explain`"), `ngrace-cli/SKILL.md:11` and `:18`, and their mirrors. `bun ./src/grace.ts explain change-spec` prints the root usage — the fifteen dispatched roots (`src/grace.ts:42-57`) contain no `explain`. The live form is `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --explain change-spec`, which prints the shape reference, and the same skill writes that full form once at `ngrace-spec/SKILL.md:109` — so the file teaches the flag correctly in one sentence and as a bare token in another. The executor spent a probe discovering the real argv; the authority's brief repeated the skill's form (`ngrace explain`) and is on the brief's WRONG ledger for it.
**Why the token form exists.** `F61` forbids two adjacent hyphens inside an XML comment body, and the artifact rules say "name argv tokens" for that reason — but a `SKILL.md` is markdown, not XML, and the same file already writes `--explain` in prose. The abbreviation was carried from the artifact rule into a surface that never needed it, and it dropped the one fact that makes the token usable: which command carries it.
**The rule.** A skill that names a CLI token names the command that takes it, in the form the shell accepts (`lint --explain <code|shape>`); the bare-token idiom is for XML artifact bodies only. Applies to every "argv token `x`" sentence in the skills — measure the population before the fix, not this one line.
Owner: the next teaching-surface increment (with [F236](#f236), [F237](#f237), [F238](#f238)); every one of the twelve lines is in scope by name, canonical and mirror.

Finding.Title: ### F241 — `ngrace-plan` says to list every inevitable path in `ObservedWriteScope` and never says that a not-yet-existing module-ownable `src/` path is a lint error from plan-approve until the creating task lands: the third bundle to walk into the window, the first to measure it as a skill gap rather than a brief's error. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-12 at `34072ef`** by the executor authoring `C-APPLY-VERB/plan.xml` under `ngrace-plan` with no rules in the brief, reported in `SKILL GAPS` and re-driven by the authority. `must_do` 6 ("list that path at plan time — never leave the executor choosing between a scope breach and a failed task") is right and complete about *what* to list; the plan that follows it carries `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` (`src/lint/core.ts:740-773`) on `src/grace-apply.ts` and `src/test-support/c-apply-verb-close-evidence.ts` at `draft` and at `approved` — 2 errors, lint exit 1, `--parallel-preflight` exit 1, `--assertions baseline` exit 1 — until T-001 and T-006 create the files with the `LINKS:` owner. Nothing in the skill says the error is expected, that `gate approve` does not see it, that the approval commit names it (`D12`, `F19`), or that the executor's baseline run will exit non-zero for a reason that is not a baseline failure.
**History.** `F62` (`C-SCHEMA-REFERENCE`) and `F119` (`C-SUPERSEDE-VERB`) recorded the same code, each time as the authority's brief ending "stop when lint is green". Both findings blamed the brief; the skill that the brief was standing in for was never amended, so a brief-less dispatch reproduces the gap exactly. The precedent for the window's form survives only in a squash commit body (`13a8a45`), which no executor reads.
**The rule** (one sentence for `must_do` 6 or `command_phase_rules`): a module-ownable `src/` path in `ObservedWriteScope` that does not exist yet errors `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` at every lint mode until the task that creates it lands with the owning `LINKS:`; the plan is still approved, the approval commit names the predicted error, and the executor's baseline exit reflects it.
Owner: the next teaching-surface increment (with [F236](#f236), [F237](#f237), [F238](#f238), [F239](#f239)). Neighbour to F62, F119.

Finding.Title: ### F185 — a real-repository measurement test has no explicit timeout, so archiving the 70th bundle turned the suite red after the move. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-06**, during the close of `C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY`, post-archive.
`src/grace-context.test.ts:522` calls `buildTaskSlice` against the live package root for three named archive subjects. It carries **no explicit timeout**, so it inherits Bun's 5000 ms default. The `git mv` that archived this bundle took the archive from 69 to 70 directories, and the test now runs **~5240 ms**. Deterministic, not flaky: three consecutive isolated runs failed at 5236.80 / 5243.60 / 5245.86 ms.
**It is purely a timeout; nothing is logically wrong.** Probed in the discriminating direction: `bun test --timeout 20000` gives **1735 pass / 3 skip / 0 fail**, exit 0, with every assertion in that test holding. The product is correct and the suite is red only against the default clock.
**This is exactly [F100](#f100)'s class, and the two-verdict close is what caught it.** The executor's `bun test` was green and honest — it ran **before** the archive move. The failure exists only after it. A single-verdict close would have archived this bundle with a red suite and never displayed the criteria whose `CloseEvidence` is `bun test`.
**The defect is structural, not incidental.** A test whose purpose is to measure the *real* repository has a cost that necessarily grows with the repository, so a fixed default clock is the wrong constraint for it — and any bundle archived from here would have tripped it, independent of this one. The remedy is an explicit, generous timeout on that `it(...)`, not a fixture rewrite, which would destroy the measurement the test exists to take.
**It did not block the close, and the authority's first reading that it did was wrong.** Bare `bun test` is **not** a `CloseEvidence` command for this bundle; the criteria run `bun test <file>` against three named `scripts/*.test.ts` files, none of which is `grace-context.test.ts`. All fifteen `CloseEvidence` commands were re-run after the `git mv` and exit 0.
**The fix had to land after the close, not inside it.** `AC-NO-GRAMMAR`'s evidence is `git diff --exit-code <base> -- src/`, so any `src/` write inside the bundle fails it — the one-line timeout edit was applied, tripped that criterion, was reverted for the verdict, and re-applied as its own commit once the bundle was archived. The criterion's prose targets the grammar layer (`src/artifact/xml.ts`, `xml-serialize.ts`) but its command is repository-wide over `src/`; anyone writing a bundle that may need an incidental `src/` fix during close should scope that command to the files the prose actually names.

Finding.Title: ### F198 — `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` archived without a registry row, so the finding it settled is still live and cannot be paid. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-08** at `54e26d9`, during the `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION` spec review, from the executor's `WRONG` field against the authority's brief.
[F172](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml) is **live** (`findings.xml:7155`) and describes the citation validator's qualifier-suffix slug grammar — a mechanism that **no longer exists**. `expectedSlugFor` and `duplicateCount` are absent from `src/` and `scripts/` (0 hits), and the citation validator's only duplicate rule is `duplicate-id` over **index ids**, not tokens across layers. A split-token fixture drives all three record validators to exit 0. The mechanism was removed by `67bc55c` — `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2`, PR #74.
**The bundle that settled it has no row.** `grep -c '<Row name="C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2"'` returns **0** in `registry.xml` and **0** in `registry-retired.xml`, while the first `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT` has one. `derivePayerMap` keys payments on chartered rows gated on `archive.has(row.name)`, so a bundle with no row pays nothing: `F172` cannot become eligible by any path, and the live genre carries a finding whose subject was deleted two bundles ago.
**This is [F187](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml)'s class surviving the bundle chartered to end it.** `C-PAYMENT-RECORD` recorded the payments that already happened; this is at least one it did not record. The population it missed is unmeasured here and must not be guessed — measuring it is part of the remedy, not a premise of it.
**Why it did not ride in `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION`**, stated so the deferral is not silent: paying `F172` means creating a row for an already-archived bundle, whose `name` equals an archive directory on sight, and deciding what else `C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2` settled. That is a population audit and a placement question, neither of which that bundle's approved scope answers, and grafting them in would contradict its own NonGoals. Surfaced to the maintainer as a charter candidate rather than filed.
Owner: the next charter decision.
**Cost already paid.** The authority's first spec brief carried `F172`'s headline as present behaviour, and the spec it produced repeated the claim in a Constraint until the executor measured it. A finding is never evidence of present state.

Finding.Title: ### F197 — a finding can be paid by a sentence: `derivePayerMap` mints payments from prose, not only from `Pays`. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-08** at `54e26d9`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:466-497`, raised by the executor's `WRONG` field against the authority's claim that a row without `Pays` leaves a finding with no path out.
Beyond the `Pays` field of a chartered row, two prose paths mint payments:
- `closedWithTokens(row.statusText)` over an archived chartered row's `StatusText`, gated on the row's name being an archive directory; - a pass over **every** archived `spec.xml` that pays every `F`-token appearing in any sentence matching `PAID_FINDING_RE`.
**The consequence.** Eligibility is what `D28` and `D28.1` make the enforcement, and it can be minted by wording. An ordinary sentence in an archived spec that happens to match the pattern marks the findings it names as paid, and they become eligible for retirement on the next `--retire`. Nothing declares the payment; a phrase does.
**Observed cost, not theorised.** `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION`'s spec carries a guard clause asserting that its own prose contains no sentence matching that pattern — a spec defending itself against its own text being read as a payment. That is the tax this path imposes on every future spec.
Owner: a later bundle. The remedy is a design question — narrow the prose paths to an explicit declaration, or keep them and make the derivation report what it minted and from which sentence — and the authority has no position yet.

Finding.Title: ### F244 — the `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY clamp invariant` test asserts `headroom < 7 × median` on the production record, a relation the ratified engine falsifies by construction on any clamped move that frees room: latent since it shipped, red on the first bundle that retires enough. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-12 at `af0f721`, by the executor authoring `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY`'s spec and re-driven by the authority.** `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:3067` reads the production `findings.xml`, computes `7 × median(live element lines)` and asserts the persisted `headroom` is below it ("the clamp binds"). The engine's ratified arithmetic (`C-ROOT-WINDOW-2`/`-3`: persisted ceiling = `min(previous ceiling, pre-move base + floored headroom)`, `persistSnapshot` with `ceilingBase = findingsBaseRead`) computes the formula ceiling from the **pre-move** base so that a retire frees the moved lines; when the clamp binds, `headroom = 7 × median + lines moved`, which is never below the product. Driven on a whole-repository copy of this bundle's state: mid-bundle `7597/249/7846` against 238; post-close `7569/266/7835` against 238 — `expect(headroom).toBeLessThan(product)` fails both times. It stayed green through every close since `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY` only because the held ceiling kept `ceiling − base` under the product while the live file grew; the first bundle to retire three findings without flushing any crossed it.
**The class.** [F225](#f225), [F229](#f229), [F232](#f232), [F237](#f237), [F238](#f238): an assertion describing the state at its own bundle's approval, written as an invariant. The two relations beside it (`base + headroom = ceiling`, `base = newlineCount`) are durable and already asserted by the `C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4` roots-invariant tripwire.
Owner: `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` repairs it (the clause removed; the test deleted or renamed so no test claims a clamp it does not assert); its payment is recorded at this entry's flush by appending `F244` to that bundle's retired row, the retired-row append the same bundle establishes as lawful for `F185`. Neighbour to [F225](#f225), [F237](#f237).

Finding.Title: ### F222 — the anti-occupancy guard is a ratchet against drift, not an adversarial control, and no artifact says which. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
`C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3` rebuilt the guard over the TypeScript parser and closed the three failures its charter named: a number hidden behind an internal semicolon, a false red on an `async` reformat, and blindness to destructured and non-first declarators. It conforms to that charter exactly. Eight other ways to put a number back are silent, and the charter never claimed otherwise.
**Measured 2026-09-10 against the delivered `src/artifact/xml.test.ts`, on a throwaway copy of the repository, each mutation driven through `bun test src/artifact/xml.test.ts` with the exit code read directly.** The suite is 35 pass / 0 fail — the guard silent — for every one of: a module-scope alias (`const A = 195; const B = A;` with `B` referenced from the body, so no binding both carries the literal and is referenced); a module-scope `function` returning the number; a `class` static property; an `enum` member; a BigInt literal (`195n`, a `BigIntLiteral` node, not a `NumericLiteral`) inside the guarded body; a field typed through an alias (`type Num = number`); a computed property name (`["expected"]`); and a union-typed field (`expected: number | undefined`). The control discriminates: a plain `expected: number` interface member fires, 34 pass / 1 fail. The silences are the guard's real behaviour, not a broken probe.
**None of the eight is a defect against the delivered work.** The spec's Goal R3 enumerates the duties by shape — duty (iii) is scoped to "every declarator of a **module-scope variable statement** … the initializer examined in full as an expression node", and an aliased binding has no numeric initializer while a `function`, `class` or `enum` is not a variable statement; duty (ii) is scoped to "a member named `expected` typed `number`", and an alias is not the `number` keyword; duty (i) reads "the parser's numeric-literal nodes", which a BigInt is not. The implementation matches its charter shape for shape. The gap is in the charter.
**Deferred, with the conflict D11 requires.** The duties are enumerated in an approved, frozen spec, so widening them means a third `ngrace supersede` in this lineage, at depth 3 — and every one of the eight paths requires a deliberate, unusual construction. None is a drift path: the next flush that wants to re-pin a count writes `toBe(211)` (duty i), restores the table (duty ii), or adds `const EXPECTED = 211` (duty iii), and the guard holds against all three. Superseding a conformant bundle to harden against intent is disproportionate, and the alternative — quietly widening a duty because the fix is small — is the failure mode [F25](#f25) names and the contract exists to prevent.
**The follow-on must decide the question before it writes any code.** If the guard is a ratchet against accidental drift, it is already correct and what is owed is one sentence in the artifact saying so, in the house "known boundary, stated rather than hidden" form the same spec already uses for its over-approximate reference semantics — the boundary is currently unstated, which is the only part a future reader could mistake. If it is meant to resist intent, it needs a different design: alias chains of arbitrary depth, every declaration form and every type spelling put it in an arms race a scan over source text cannot win, and the honest instrument would be a check on the values the test compares rather than the syntax it is written in. Choosing the second without saying so is how a guard acquires a reputation it cannot support.
**The absence is searched, not assumed.** `adversar|evasion|evade|arms race|deliberate construction` over this bundle's spec and plan, over all six record genre files live and retired, and over the delivered `src/artifact/xml.test.ts`, on 2026-09-10: two hits, both in the spec, and both the word "evasion" used as the label of the R3-a probe rather than a statement of what the guard is for. `adversar` and `arms race` appear nowhere in the record. The word "ratchet" appears there eight times, all of them about the citation index's one-way ceiling that `C-INDEX-METRIC-2` broke, none about this guard. No artifact states the guard's threat model in either direction.
Disposition: **first item of the follow-on queue**, ahead of [F216](#f216) and [F221](#f221), and it takes the same file as `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY-3`, so it is sequential rather than file-disjoint — it cannot ride alongside. Owner: a chartered bundle. Neighbour to [F25](#f25) (the deferral form this entry follows) and [F220](#f220) (a design ratified on principle and never driven).

Finding.Title: ### F223 — the guard's subtree walk has no early exit and keeps traversing after it has found the node. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
`visitSubtree` recurses through `ts.forEachChild` unconditionally, so the callback-locating walk continues over every remaining node in the file after the target has already been bound. The match logic short-circuits on `found !== undefined`, so no second match can overwrite the first and there is no behavioural difference — this is wasted traversal only, on a file that is currently 959 lines and grows with every synthetic direction added. Read from the recursion structure, not driven: there is no observable behaviour to construct a fixture around, which is also why it is cosmetic.
Owner: the same chartered bundle as [F222](#f222) — same file, same functions, and no reason to open the file twice.

Finding.Title: ### F240 — `review.confidently-wrong` fires on every active plan's Target `MustExist` of a file the plan itself creates, so a file-creating bundle carries review errors from plan-approve until its first task lands: F123's open question, the active-plan half. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-12 at `34072ef`, plan-approve of `C-APPLY-VERB`.** `bun ./src/grace.ts review --path . --change C-APPLY-VERB` → 3 errors, all `review.confidently-wrong`, on `plan.xml`'s Target `MustExist` of `src/grace-apply.ts`, `src/grace-apply.test.ts` and `src/test-support/c-apply-verb-close-evidence.ts` — the three files the bundle exists to create. `src/review/core.ts:505-537` walks every `plan.xml` under `active/` and `archive/`, skips only `superseded | rejected | cancelled` roots, walks `MustExist` anywhere via `walkNodes` (Baseline and Target alike), and has no exemption for a path the plan's own `ObservedWriteScope` declares. A Target assertion is the end state; reading it against present disk before execution is a category error the detector's name makes explicit. The precedent's ledger confirms the cost is silent: `C-SUPERSEDE-COMMAND/run-ledger.xml` mentions `confidently-wrong` zero times — the findings stood at plan-approve, vanished when `src/grace-supersede.ts` landed, and were never acked, so the record shows a clean review that was never clean at approval.
**Relation to `F123`.** F123 recorded the same detector on a *superseded* plan's targets and left open whether the audit should skip superseded roots. This is the other half: an active plan's Target `MustExist` is a claim about the future by definition, and the walk should read Baseline against disk and Target against the applied state — or skip Target for plans whose `ObservedWriteScope` names the path. Neighbour to F123.
Owner: the bundle that next opens `src/review/core.ts`, sequenced by the maintainer (`C-APPLY-VERB` excludes new `review.*` code by its spec, F101). Until then, plan-approve reviews of file-creating bundles carry these errors and the approval commit names them.

Finding.Title: ### F245 — the review's identity skip covers a bundle's own `spec.xml` and `plan.xml` but not its `design-context.xml`, so a bundle that writes the optional companion the `ngrace-spec` skill defines is reported out of scope and must declare its own artifact in `ObservedWriteScope`. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-13 at `d84e37a`, by the executor authoring `C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY/plan.xml` under `ngrace-plan`.** The first `bun ./src/grace.ts review --path . --change C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY` exited 1 with `review.scope-outside-write-scope .ngrace/changes/active/C-PAYMENT-INTEGRITY/design-context.xml`; declaring the file in `ObservedWriteScope` made the re-run 0 findings. `isReviewedChangeSpecOrPlanPath` (`src/review/core.ts:1037`) skips exactly four paths — the reviewed change's active and archived `spec.xml` and `plan.xml` — while `ngrace-spec`'s `change_bundle_contract` names `design-context.xml` as the bundle's third artifact and `ngrace-plan` `must_do` row 15 lists only `spec.xml`, `plan.xml` and `decisions.md` as the expected scope findings. The plan's declaration is a route-around: a bundle listing its own authoring artifact as a write it observed, to satisfy an audit that already exempts its two siblings by identity.
**The rule.** The identity skip covers every artifact the bundle contract defines for the reviewed change, or row 15 says which of them must be declared and why. Owner: whoever next opens `src/review/core.ts` (with [F240](#f240)) for the skip; the next teaching-surface increment for row 15. Neighbour to [F236](#f236) (row 15's ground).

Finding.Title: ### F243 — a task's `Verification` `git diff --exit-code` written cumulatively from the base commit is red at the stage it claims unless it excludes every earlier task's files, and nothing can notice: task `Verification` commands are checked for non-emptiness and never executed. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-12 at `f0bbab7`, executing `C-FLUSH-AND-TEACH`.** T-002's and T-003's `Verification` carry `git diff --exit-code <base> -- skills/ src/ scripts/ … ':(exclude)…'` naming that task's own writes as excludes but not `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, which T-001 wrote first; at T-002's stage both commands exit 1 on T-001's walk. Adding the one exclusion makes each exit 0 (the executor's measurement, re-driven). The plan was approved with the defect because the planner drove every `Verification` command at HEAD, before execution, where every cumulative diff is trivially green — `ngrace-plan` `must_do` 19 says "drive every planned command on a prototype" and does not say *in the state the task leaves*.
**Why no gate saw it.** `src/artifact/grammar.ts:2274` requires a task's `Verification` to hold at least one non-empty `Command`; no lint mode, `--run-commands` (which evaluates `MustPassCommand` assertions only) or cursor verb executes them. A task's `Verification` is prose to the product: its pass is the executor's claim, and the `command-run` events the ledger holds are the assertion commands, not the task's. The two red commands cost nothing at execution and nothing at close; they are wrong in an immutable artifact, and a supersede for a pathspec is the disproportion `F236` names.
**The rule.** A per-task byte-invariance command excludes every earlier task's files, or is scoped to the paths the task itself must not touch rather than everything-but-mine; and a planned `Verification` command is driven in the tree state its task leaves, not at HEAD. Whether the product should execute task `Verification` at `attempt pass` is a design question this entry records and does not answer.
Owner: the next teaching-surface increment (`ngrace-plan` row 19, beside the clause `C-FLUSH-AND-TEACH` added); the execution question to a chartered bundle. Neighbour to [F236](#f236), [F237](#f237).

Finding.Title: ### F246 — an approved plan's `BaselineAssertions` `MustNotContain` was false at HEAD from the moment of approval, and nothing on the approval path evaluates a draft plan's baseline assertions: lint, review and the approve gate were green, root lint went red at the gate's status write, and the executor halted at the selected baseline with zero code written. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-13 at `d1aa693`, by the executor at the `C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE` selected-baseline preflight.** The approved plan carried `<MustNotContain><File>src/review/core.ts</File><Text>if (scopeIdentityFromPlanRel(planRel)?.planLocation !== "active") continue;</Text></MustNotContain>` as a baseline needle for `detectConfidentlyWrong`. `evaluateTextContainment` (`src/artifact/assertions.ts:386-409`) decides by `contents.includes` over the whole file, and the string occurs at `src/review/core.ts:589` (`detectSelfReferential`) and `:824` (`detectZeroOrMoreSwallow`) — the `C-REVIEW-ARCHIVE-SCOPE` location filters the plan's own NonGoals forbid touching. So the needle could never be true: `lint --path .` and `--assertions baseline --run-commands` exit 1 with one `assertion.MustNotContain`, while `--assertions final` (target only) does not see it and the close would not have been blocked. Before `gate approve` the same tree linted 0/0 (draft plans' baseline assertions are not evaluated), `ngrace review --change` reported 0 findings, and the gate permitted; the authority read the needle, approved, committed, and never ran root lint after the status write. The property the needle restated already lives, correctly scoped, at `src/review/core.test.ts:3756` (a source slice bounded to the function).
**The class.** [F42](#f42): a baseline `MustNotContain` needle must be a string only the implementation can introduce — a whole-file containment on a spelling that other functions share is a pin on the wrong position. Neighbour to [F211](#f211) but not its window: F211's baselines are true at HEAD and flip at the first write; this one was false at approval. Remedy taken: D27 — `ngrace spec new C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2`, `ngrace supersede` (folded epoch 1: opened, eight `command-run`, pause, discarded), the `-2` artifacts re-authored from the archived bytes with the needle removed. Cost: two ratifications and two dispatches, zero code, the `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION` profile.
**The rule, three surfaces.** (1) `ngrace-plan` row 19 drives planned *commands*; a plan's baseline `MustContain` / `MustNotContain` needles are evaluated by nothing before approval — the plan skill states that every baseline needle is driven with `--assertions baseline` on the approved-shaped copy, and that a `MustNotContain` on a shared spelling is bounded to a test slice, never a whole file. (2) `ngrace-execute`'s recovery table has no row for "an approved plan's own baseline assertion is false at HEAD"; the executor inferred hard-stop from rule 11 — the row is written. (3) The authority runs root lint after every `gate approve` and before the approval commit: the gate's status write is what turns the baseline evaluation on. Owner: the next teaching increment (V2) for (1) and (2); (3) is the authority's standing rule from this date.

Finding.Title: ### F247 — four copies per tree of one skill sentence, across three skills, say a bundle's own `spec.xml` and `plan.xml` are *expected* `review.scope-outside-write-scope` findings at plan-approve; the shipped identity skip silences both, only `decisions.md` fires, and `ngrace-plan` row 15's own second half already says so. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-13 at `3bbc8ed`, `4096e15` and `52b8ba4`** — by the executor on three dispatches and by the authority's subagent at the plan-approve of `C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE`: `ngrace review --path . --change C-… --changed-files spec.xml,plan.xml` → `No out-of-scope paths`; adding `decisions.md` → exactly one finding, on `decisions.md`; the real plan-approve reviews of both `C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE` plans reported 0 findings over 3 changed files. The sentence — "At plan-approve `review.scope-outside-write-scope` on the bundle's own spec.xml, plan.xml, and (when that file changed) decisions.md is expected; do not add those paths to ObservedWriteScope" — stands in `skills/ngrace/ngrace-spec/SKILL.md` twice (`status_rules` `:28`, `workflow` step 6 `:133`), in `skills/ngrace/ngrace-reviewer/SKILL.md` once (`mechanized_first` `:37`; first staged as `review_judgment`, a label carried from a report unchecked), and in `skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md` row 15 (`:70`), where the same row then says — eight occurrences with the packaged mirror, measured by the executor's whole-tree grep after the authority's two-file grep had staged "three" (F138's class) — "the review already skips the bundle's own `spec.xml` and `plan.xml` by identity" — one row contradicting itself. None of the three skills names `design-context.xml`, which [F245](#f245)'s bundle (`C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2`, PR #95) added to the skip.
**The rule.** The sentence states what the product does: the reviewed bundle's own `spec.xml`, `plan.xml` and `design-context.xml` are identity-skipped in both locations and are never declared; `decisions.md` is reported and is expected only when that file changed. One sentence, in all four places, and the mirror. Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F248 — the selected-assertion commands the skills list have preconditions the skills never state: `--assertions baseline|target --run-commands` refuses until an epoch is open on a declared task, and `--assertions target` refuses a plan that is not yet approved; both were learned from the tool's refusals, on three dispatches. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-13** by the executor at the `C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE` execution (`d1aa693`) and both `-2` drives (`52b8ba4`, `c3d8798`): `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --change C-… --assertions baseline --run-commands` on an approved plan with no open epoch → exit 1, `Cannot record command-run: no declared task is in scope. Use cursor advance on a declared T-NNN…` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:3424`); after `cursor advance --change C-… --task T-001 --open-epoch` → exit 0. `--assertions target --change C-…` on a draft plan → `assertion.change-not-approved`, exit 1. `ngrace-execute` `<assertion_commands>` and `ngrace-plan` `<validation>` list the commands and say nothing of either precondition; `ngrace-plan` row 19 tells the author to drive every planned command before approval and gives no procedure that would survive the first refusal. Sequenced as rule 12 in `ngrace-execute` (open the epoch before the baseline) but not as a precondition of the command itself, and absent from `ngrace-plan` entirely.
**The rule.** Each listed assertion command carries its precondition beside it: `--run-commands` needs an open epoch on a declared task; `target` and `final` need an approved plan; the plan skill's row 19 says how to drive them on an approved-shaped copy (`gate approve --artifact plan` on the copy, then `cursor advance --open-epoch`). Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F249 — a freshly minted `ngrace spec new` skeleton fails `validate:ci`: `check-teaching-surface` refuses it for the docs-and-examples decision it does not carry, so the repository is CI-red between the mint and the author's rewrite, and the skill that calls the skeleton "a starting shape" never says so. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-13 at `370ed79`** by the authority: `ngrace spec new C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2` then `bun run validate:ci` → exit 1, `refusal: … C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2/spec.xml — docs-and-examples decision (a Goal, Constraint or NonGoal decides README.md and examples/): missing` (`scripts/check-teaching-surface.ts:272`, `checkDocsAndExamplesDecision` `:259`); the skeleton contains 0 occurrences of `README` or `examples` (`git show 370ed79:.ngrace/changes/active/C-REVIEW-SELF-SCOPE-2/spec.xml`). After the executor's rewrite `validate:ci` exited 0. `ngrace-spec` `shape_sources` says the skeleton "is a starting shape, not a verdict" and `docs_and_examples` says "Silence fails" — true of the artifact, unstated of the mint.
**The rule, two surfaces.** Teaching: the skill says the mint alone is CI-red until the rewrite decides `README.md` and `examples/`, so a mint is never committed bare. Product: the skeleton seeds a docs-and-examples `<NonGoal>` placeholder the author must replace, or `check-teaching-surface` exempts a skeleton still at `AC-SKELETON`. Owner: the next teaching increment for the sentence; whoever next opens `spec new`'s template (the D38 bundle touches it) for the seed.

Finding.Title: ### F250 — the attempt-pair audit pairs only the *last* fail per task with the next pass, so a task that records two red-first pairs as fail, fail, pass, pass has one fail never audited and one pass never paired; the review reported "2 fail→pass pair(s)" over a ledger holding four. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-14 at `7ef317c`, the close of `C-TEACH-DRIVE-BEFORE-APPROVE-2`.** The plan's T-001 and T-002 each carry two red-first pairs; the executor recorded them as attempts 10 fail (`flush-invariant`), 11 fail (`record-row`), 12 pass, 13 pass, and 15 fail (`teaching-needles`), 16 fail (`stale-scan`), 17 pass, 18 pass — each fail in its own round trip with its own `WriteEvidence`, honest by construction. `ngrace review --change` → `Attempt-pair audit: ran over 2 fail→pass pair(s)`. `src/review/core.ts:1466-1488` builds pairs with `lastFailByTask`: a fail overwrites the previous fail for the task, the next pass pairs with that one and clears it, and a pass with no pending fail is skipped — so 11→12 and 16→17 were audited, 10 and 15 never were, 13 and 18 paired with nothing. The `review.attempt-pair-identical-tree` guard (C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY) therefore covers half of a two-pair task, and a fabricated first pair would pass the audit unread. The authority read the four `WriteEvidence` lists by hand for this bundle.
**The rule, two surfaces.** Product: the audit pairs every fail with the next pass *for that signature key* (or every fail in order with the passes that follow), so two consecutive reds are two audited pairs; a pass with no fail to pair stays a finding. Teaching: until then, `ngrace-execute` says a task with more than one red-first pair interleaves them — fail A, pass A, fail B, pass B — so each pair is audited. Owner: whoever next opens `src/review/core.ts` for the audit; the next teaching increment for the sentence.

Finding.Title: ### F251 — `spec new` resolves the branch it hashes from the *process cwd*'s git, not from `--path`: a mint run from inside repository A against `--path <repository B>` folds A's branch into B's bundle id, silently. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-14 at the close of `C-HASHED-BUNDLE-IDS-2` (`f5d1362`), by the authority's probe.** `resolveBranch` in `src/grace-generate.ts` falls through `--branch` and `NGRACE_SPEC_BRANCH` to `execFileSync("git", ["rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD"])` with no `cwd` option, so git answers for the shell's working directory. Driven: from a copy of this repository with no `.git` and `NGRACE_SPEC_BRANCH` unset, `spec new NOBRANCH --timestamp … --path <temp project>` refused (`spec new requires --branch, NGRACE_SPEC_BRANCH, or a git working tree.`) although the flag names a project — the tool never looked under `--path`; the converse (a git cwd and a gitless `--path`) mints with the cwd's branch. D38's hash is "a one-way hash of the branch name and a timestamp"; the spec's Constraint names `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` without saying where. Every drive this session ran from the project root, where the two coincide, which is why nothing measured it.
**The rule.** The branch is read from the project the mint writes into — `execFileSync` with `cwd` set to the resolved root — and the `mint:` line already prints the branch it used, so a reader can see it. A one-line change with one test: a mint from a foreign cwd against a `--path` on another branch hashes the `--path` branch. Owner: the next opener of `src/grace-generate.ts`.

Finding.Title: ### F253 — `ngrace-plan` is silent on three things the plan of the first hashed-id bundle had to learn by driving: a `--assertions baseline` run over `MustPassCommand`s needs `--run-commands` and an open epoch, selected-assertion commands need `--change`, and a faithful post-close copy needs `.ngrace/scratch`. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-14 across the plan and execution dispatches of `C-PAIR-AUDIT-MINT-CWD-1-ED6B7D22` (executor `SKILL GAPS` and `WRONG`, re-driven by the authority).** (1) `<validation>` (line 116) and row 19 (line 74) name `--run-commands` beside `--assertions target`/`final` only; a baseline run of a plan carrying twelve `MustPassCommand`s without it returns exit 1 with twelve `assertion.command-not-evaluated` errors that read like breakage; with `--run-commands` inside an open epoch it is green. The authority's plan brief carried the same omission. (2) The approved plan's T-005 criterion wrote `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --assertions target` — the CLI refuses `assertion.change-required … requires one --change C-* identifier`; the skill's assertion rows never say `--change` is required, and the prose slipped past approval because no instrument reads criterion prose. (3) Row 19's "faithful post-close copy" does not say the copy must carry `.ngrace/scratch`: without it, `review.confidently-wrong` fires six times on archived plans whose `BaselineAssertions` `MustExist` the buffer path (measured on two copies), and a planner reads six defects the production tree does not show. Also measured: the `spec_plan_traceability` sentence "each task that implements one should list it under `Satisfies`" reads against the later rule that close-bound criteria are never `Satisfies` targets; with sixteen of seventeen criteria close-bound, the first sentence is the trap.
**The rule.** Four sentences in `ngrace-plan`: baseline drives carry `--run-commands` inside an open epoch on an approved-shaped copy; every selected-assertion command names `--change`; the post-close copy carries `.ngrace/scratch` read-only; `Satisfies` maps only criteria without `CloseEvidence`. Each pinned by a `TAUGHT_RULES` needle. Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F254 — `ngrace-execute` has no rule for a post-pass correction to an earlier task, and does not say that an `attempt` moves the cursor's current task — so a later `--run-commands` is attributed to the corrected task. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-14 on the ledger of `C-PAIR-AUDIT-MINT-CWD-1-ED6B7D22` (executor fix rounds 1 and 2, verified by the authority).** After T-005 had passed, a spec-pinned remediation line was found missing from two `REVIEW_CATALOG` guides. The skill's `cursor_kinds` define `attempt` for "every verification cycle for a task" and rule 13 covers a pass-only cycle, but nothing says which task a correction attaches to, how a correction with no shipped red is recorded, or what happens to the task pointer. The executor inferred `cursor attempt` on T-001 with a `fix` signature (`catalog-remediation-gate-verdict`, fail 41 / pass 42), then a pass-only cycle for the instrument (55); each left T-001 current, so the two subsequent `--assertions target --run-commands` runs wrote their twelve `command-run` events (43–54, 56–67) under T-001 instead of T-005. Harmless to every gate, and the audit paired correctly, but the ledger now says T-001 ran the target commands twice. Both fix rounds also confirmed the remedy shape: the instrument should have been written with the criterion, so the correction would have been one honest pair instead of a driven inline red plus a pass-only cycle.
**The rule.** `ngrace-execute` gains: a correction to an already-passed task is recorded as an `attempt` on the task that owns the surface, with a `fix` signature on the fail; a pass-only correction is disclosed under rule 13; and the note that `attempt` sets the current task, so commands whose attribution matters are run after a `progress` on the intended task. Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F255 — `ngrace lint --explain <code>` answers a namespaced issue code typed without its namespace with `Unknown shape: <code>` and the shape list, so a reader who typed a code learns nothing about codes and is told to look among shapes. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-15 at `dfc5405`, by the executor authoring `C-TEACH-PLAN-DRIVES-CORRECTIONS-1-14457871` and re-driven by the authority.** `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --explain close-evidence-and-satisfied` exits 1 with `Unknown shape: close-evidence-and-satisfied` followed by `Registered shapes: artifact-root, root-metadata, …`; `--explain change.close-evidence-and-satisfied` prints the issue guide. The fallback at `src/grace-lint.ts:259` treats any argument that is not a registered code as a shape name, so the message names the wrong universe; the `ngrace-spec` skill's `shape_sources` (`ngrace lint --explain <code|shape>`) does not say that codes carry their namespace prefix, and neither does any brief form. Every catalog code carries a namespace (`change.`, `assertion.`, `review.`, …), so a bare last segment is the likeliest mis-typing.
**The rule.** When the argument matches no code and no shape, the message says both universes were searched and, when the bare argument is the last segment of exactly one registered code, names that code (`Unknown code or shape: X; did you mean change.X?`). One sentence in `ngrace-spec` `shape_sources`: issue codes are namespaced (`change.…`, `assertion.…`, `review.…`). Owner: the next opener of `src/grace-lint.ts`; the sentence, the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F256 — `review.confidently-wrong`'s `must-exist-missing` anchor key is `must-exist:<target>`, so two `MustExist` elements naming the same path in one plan emit two findings with one id; the review counts six where three ids exist, and an `--ack-finding` of one id silently covers both. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-15 at `dfc5405`, by the authority's subagent on a whole-repository copy with `.ngrace/scratch` removed.** `ngrace review --path .` exits 1 with six `review.confidently-wrong` lines carrying three distinct ids — `f9e50fe2046d7a5b` twice (`C-FLUSH-AND-REPAIR/plan.xml`), `9d745b619589d9ca` twice (`C-FLUSH-AND-UNPIN`), `44c49d73260e7cb4` twice (`C-FLUSH-TWO-WAVES`). Each plan carries the buffer path in two `MustExist` values (`C-FLUSH-AND-REPAIR/plan.xml:278` and `:328`, a baseline and a target assertion). `findingId` (`src/review/core.ts:340`) hashes `auditOrPatternId`, file, `anchorOrHunkKey`, `ruleId`; the emit site at `src/review/core.ts:547` passes `must-exist:${target}` as the anchor key with nothing that names the assertion block, so both elements hash identically. Discovered while re-driving `F253`'s third claim, which counts "six" — a count of lines, not of findings.
**The rule.** The anchor key carries the assertion's position (block kind and index, or the element's line), so two claims are two ids; or the audit de-duplicates identical claims and reports one finding with a count. Either way the review's total and its id set agree. Owner: the next opener of `src/review/core.ts`.

Finding.Title: ### F257 — a green `lint --assertions baseline|target --run-commands` report says nothing about the commands it ran: the only evidence that the `MustPassCommand`s were evaluated is the `command-run` loose events under `run/`, and a reader of the printed report cannot tell a run with commands from one without. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-15 at `43a547f` on an approved-shaped whole-repository copy of `C-TEACH-PLAN-DRIVES-CORRECTIONS-1-14457871`, by the authority.** `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --change C-… --assertions baseline --run-commands` exits 0 and prints the standard report (`Errors: 0`, `Warnings: 0`, `No issues found.`); `grep -ciE 'command' <report>` → 0. The same command without `--run-commands` exits 1 with eight `assertion.command-not-evaluated` errors (`F253`), so the red side names the commands and the green side is silent. The eight evaluations are visible only as sixteen `command-run` events (`exitCode="0"`) across two drives under the copy's `run/` directory. A report that a brief or a finding pastes as evidence of "baseline green with commands" therefore carries no such evidence in its bytes.
**The rule.** The report of a selected-assertion run states how many `MustPassCommand`s were evaluated and their exit codes (one line, `Commands: 8 evaluated, 8 exit 0`), or lists the evaluated commands under the assertion section, so the pasted tail is evidence. Owner: the next opener of `src/lint/core.ts` (the report writer) — with `F256` if the same bundle opens `src/review/core.ts`.

Finding.Title: ### F258 — a copy drive that opens its epoch with the approved `plan.xml` uncommitted puts that path into every attempt's `WriteEvidence`, and after the archive move `auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope` reddens on it: `ngrace-plan` row 19 drives a copy but never says to commit the approved plan first. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-15 at `dda5548`, on a whole-repository copy (`rsync -a`, `.git` included, `node_modules` a real directory).** A probe bundle was minted (`spec new PROBE-COPY-DRIVE`), its spec approved, and `plan new` run, leaving `plan.xml` untracked. `ngrace cursor attempt --change C-PROBE-COPY-DRIVE-1-3FD48F0F --task T-001 --outcome pass --path .` exited 0 and its event's `<WriteEvidence>` carried `.ngrace/changes/active/C-PROBE-COPY-DRIVE-1-3FD48F0F/plan.xml`. After `git add` + `git commit` of the bundle directory, a second attempt's `<WriteEvidence>` carried **no** `plan.xml` (`[]` non-`.ngrace/` files; `plan.xml in evidence: False`). The bundle directory was then moved under `.ngrace/changes/archive/`, and `ngrace review --path . --change C-PROBE-COPY-DRIVE-1-3FD48F0F` returned `Findings: 3 (errors: 2, warnings: 1, infos: 0)` with `WriteEvidence scope audit: ran over 5 path(s) … (2 finding(s))`: `review.write-evidence-outside-scope .ngrace/changes/active/C-PROBE-COPY-DRIVE-1-3FD48F0F/plan.xml — … outside ObservedWriteScope (ledger)` and the `spec.xml` twin. `auditWriteEvidenceOutsideScope` (`src/review/core.ts:1135`) exempts tool-owned lifecycle only (`run.xml` / `run-ledger.xml` / `run/**`, `isCliLifecyclePath`) and `docs/plans` (`isDocsPlansPath`) — never `plan.xml` or `spec.xml` (`:1148`–`:1152`).
**The rule.** On a copy used to reach the ceremony's state, commit the approved plan before opening the epoch: an uncommitted `plan.xml` enters every attempt's `WriteEvidence`, and after the archive move the WriteEvidence scope audit reddens on it. Section: `ngrace-plan` `must_do` row 19 (the copy-drive sentence). Token: `commit the approved plan`. Owner: the next teaching increment (this bundle's successor). `ngrace-execute` carries no copy-drive text at all, so the home is `ngrace-plan` only.

Finding.Title: ### F259 — `cursor attempt --outcome pass` accepts `--signature-kind` / `--signature-key` and silently discards them: the event carries no `FailureSignature`, so the flags a reader sees on the command line are not the record. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-15 at `dda5548`, on a whole-repository copy.** `ngrace cursor attempt --change C-PROBE-COPY-DRIVE-1-3FD48F0F --task T-001 --outcome pass --signature-kind test --signature-key probe-key --path .` exited 0 (`Attempt 1 for T-001: pass`) and the written event `run/2-T-001-attempt.xml` is `<NgraceRunEvent outcome="pass" … kind="attempt"><WriteEvidence …/></NgraceRunEvent>` — `grep -c FailureSignature` over the file is **0**. `recordAttempt` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:1940`) pushes `failureSignatureNode` only under `options.outcome === "fail" && options.signature` (`:2000`); a `pass` with a signature is neither refused nor recorded.
**The rule.** A signature passed on a pass is discarded: `--signature-kind` and `--signature-key` are accepted on `pass`, but the event carries no `FailureSignature` — supply them only on `fail`. Section: `ngrace-execute` `cursor_kinds` kind `attempt`, the "How to emit" line. Token: `the event carries no`. Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F260 — after `ngrace supersede`, the successor's plan is authored from the archived predecessor's `plan.xml` (which stays `status="superseded"` with `<Replacement>`) with the id changed where it is data, and neither `ngrace-plan` `approved_plan_immutability` nor `ngrace-spec` says so. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-15 at `dda5548` over the archive.** The predecessor `C-TEACH-PLAN-DRIVES-CORRECTIONS-1-14457871/plan.xml` and its successor `C-TEACH-PLAN-DRIVES-CORRECTIONS-2-1E59AEAA/plan.xml` each carry the bundle id **19** times; normalizing each id to `<ID>` and diffing shows the successor is the predecessor's plan with the wrapper id changed where the id is data, plus carried-forward content. `ngrace-plan` `approved_plan_immutability` names only "create the replacement with `ngrace spec new --supersedes <C-PRED>`, then run `ngrace supersede`" — it does not say the successor's artifacts may be authored from the archived draft; `ngrace-spec` says nothing about it either. (The archived predecessor's plan is the only copy of that draft: `ngrace supersede` moves it, it is never re-minted.)
**The rule.** After `ngrace supersede`, author the successor's artifacts from the archived predecessor's draft, changing the id where it is data — the archived plan is the source, and an approved plan is never edited in place. Section: `ngrace-plan` `approved_plan_immutability`. Token: `archived predecessor's draft`. Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F261 — `ngrace-spec` `shape_sources` names only `ngrace spec new <SLUG>`; the lineage path (`spec new --supersedes <C-PRED>`, exactly one of a bare slug or `--supersedes`, then `ngrace supersede`) is unnamed, and the verb stamps `superseded` + `<Replacement>` on the spec **and the draft plan**. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-15 at `dda5548`, on a whole-repository copy.** `ngrace spec new --supersedes C-PROBE-PRED-1-3FC34AAB --timestamp … --path .` (no slug) exited 0 and printed `mint: C-PROBE-PRED-2-C6DF5A38 slug=PROBE-PRED lineage=2 hash=C6DF5A38 …`, inheriting the predecessor's slug; `ngrace spec new PROBE-X --supersedes C-PROBE-PRED-1-3FC34AAB … --path .` refused with `spec new requires exactly one of a bare <SLUG> or --supersedes <C-PRED>.` (`spec new --help` shows `--supersedes=<supersedes> Predecessor C-* id whose slug and lineage the successor inherits`). `ngrace supersede --change C-PROBE-PRED-1-3FC34AAB --replacement C-PROBE-PRED-2-C6DF5A38 --path .` moved the bundle to `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-PROBE-PRED-1-3FC34AAB` and stamped `status="superseded"` and `<Replacement>C-PROBE-PRED-2-C6DF5A38</Replacement>` on **both** `spec.xml` and `plan.xml`. `ngrace-spec` `shape_sources` names only `ngrace spec new <SLUG>` and `status_rules` is silent on `supersede`.
**The rule.** `ngrace spec new --supersedes <C-PRED>` mints the lineage successor and requires exactly one of a bare slug or `--supersedes`; `ngrace supersede` stamps `superseded` and `<Replacement>` on the spec and the draft plan and moves the bundle. Section: `ngrace-spec` `shape_sources` and/or `status_rules`. Token: `exactly one of a bare slug`. Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F262 — no skill says `ngrace gate verdict` on the post-close copy is the evaluator of a spec's `CloseEvidence`, so executors hand-rolled readers that route around the verb. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-15 at `dda5548`, on a whole-repository copy (`rsync -a`, `.git` included, a real `node_modules`).** `grep -n defineGraceCommand src/grace.ts` and the `subCommands` map list the whole verb set — `apply, context, cursor, doctor, file, gate, graph, lint, module, plan, review, scaffold, spec, status, supersede, verification` — and no verb is *named* for extracting a spec's `<Command>` text. But `ngrace gate verdict` on an **applied-archive** bundle already evaluates every `CloseEvidence` `Command` through the shell: `evaluateCloseEvidenceChildren` (`src/gates/ledger.ts:490`) runs only when `isAppliedArchiveBundle` holds (`:485`), spawns each command with `spawnShellCommand` (`src/artifact/assertions.ts:720`, `sh -lc`), and `recordReviewVerdict` refuses `pass` when any `Result` is `fail` (`:423`–`:433`). Driven on a probe bundle archived with `ngrace apply --force --reason`: `ngrace review --change C-PROBE-GATE-VERDICT-1-AAAA1111` returned `Findings: 2 (errors: 2)` — `review.close-evidence-unevaluated` on `AC-PASS-ONE` (id `82ecf1f1963effd2`) and `AC-PASS-TWO` (id `0c35f130ac617b28`); `ngrace gate verdict --change C-PROBE-GATE-VERDICT-1-AAAA1111 --outcome pass --ack-finding 82ecf1f1963effd2 --ack-finding 0c35f130ac617b28` exited 0, and the `run-ledger.xml` `<Verdict>` carries `<AC-PASS-ONE><Exit>0</Exit><Result>pass</Result></AC-PASS-ONE>` and the `AC-PASS-TWO` twin. Planting `exit 3` in the copy's archived `AC-PASS-TWO` `CloseEvidence` made the same verb exit 1 refusing `CloseEvidence Command exited non-zero; refuse to record outcome pass.` The silence is not the verb — no skill says the verb is the evaluator, so executors wrote readers that route around it.
**The rule.** On the post-close copy, `ngrace gate verdict --change C --outcome pass` (acking the post-archive unevaluated findings) evaluates every `CloseEvidence` command through the shell, refuses `pass` on a non-zero exit, and records `Result` and `Exit` per criterion on the verdict — read them from the ledger, never from a hand-rolled reader. Section: `ngrace-plan` `must_do` row 19. Token: `never from a hand-rolled reader`. Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F263 — `src/grace-status.test.ts:1131`'s live-repo `reRatificationCount` test carries no explicit timeout and timed out at 30 230 ms on GitHub run `35017776037`; the whole-archive `collectProjectStatus(REPO_ROOT)` walk needs the repository's explicit generous timeout. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-15: the CI failure on the push of PR #100 to `main` (`dda5548`); the local re-measure at `aa97022`.** GitHub run `35017776037` failed in `src/grace-status.test.ts:1131` — `it("live repo reports measured reRatificationCount table, both keys as numbers, and measured chain depths")` — with `(fail) … live repo reports … [30230.55ms]` and `^ this test timed out after 30000ms.` (`gh run view 35017776037 --log-failed | grep -E 'timed out|reRatificationCount'`; the pair appears twice, once per validate step). The test calls `collectProjectStatus(REPO_ROOT)` over the whole archive (`ls -d .ngrace/changes/archive/*/ | wc -l` = **106**) and carries no explicit timeout (`grep -c '}, [0-9_]*);' src/grace-status.test.ts` = **0**). Driven locally with a generous timeout: `bun test --timeout=120000 src/grace-status.test.ts -t "live repo reports"` → `1 pass` in `[9811.89ms]`, wall clock `9.905s` — the walk is green, so the CI failure is the 30 s default, not the assertion.
**The rule.** A test driven against this repository's real archive carries an explicit generous timeout, because the walk scales with the archive and Bun's 30 s default is not generous. The house in-code form is `}, 60_000);` (the record suite uses it fourteen times); the CLI form is `--timeout=120000` (the determinism chain). Section: `src/grace-status.test.ts:1131` (the `it` gains the timeout). Owner: this bundle (`C-STATUS-TEST-TIMEOUT-*`).

Finding.Title: ### F242 — `tsconfig.json` includes only `src/**`, so every `scripts/*.test.ts` is never typechecked: `bun run typecheck` is green while the retirement suite carries three type errors at HEAD and Bun strips the types at run time. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-12 at `f975508` + the `C-APPLY-VERB` execution tree.** `tsconfig.json` → `"include": ["src/**/*.ts"]`. `bunx tsc --noEmit` exit 0. Running tsc directly on `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (`--ignoreConfig --strict --types bun-types --moduleResolution bundler`) → **3 errors at HEAD** (lines 2607, 3821, 4082 — `toBe(string | undefined)`), and the delivered T-006 row walk added **5 more** in one declaration: `rows` typed `{ file, attrs: Record<string,string>, … }` while every push wrote `{ file, status, kind, … }` and every read took `row.status` / `row.kind`. The suite was green (93 pass) because Bun strips types; the authority fixed the declaration (one line, disclosed in the close commit).
