The two other touched scripts suites (`skill-contracts`, `release-check`) typecheck clean.
**The class.** `F125` measured the same gap for `src/`: a green `bun test` on code that did not typecheck, caught only because `validate:ci` runs `typecheck`. That repair covered `src/`; `scripts/` — where the record engine, its 93-test suite, the release check and the teaching-surface check live — was never brought under it, so `F125`'s guard is silent on the directory that most of the governed-path work has landed in since.
**The rule.** `typecheck` covers every TypeScript file the suite runs: extend `include` to `scripts/**/*.ts` (and fix the three existing errors in the same change), or add a second tsconfig for `scripts/` wired into `validate:ci`. A green typecheck that does not read the file under test is `F125` with a narrower premise.
Owner: a chartered bundle, sequenced by the maintainer; `.ngrace-lint.json` already names `scripts/` adoption as deferred to a later `C-*`, and this rides with it or ahead of it. Neighbour to F125.

Finding.Title: ### F264 — the approved `C-SCRIPTS-ADOPTION-1-F621B7C0` spec forbids every `src/` write while the deliverable forces one: `src/grace-lint.test.ts:1930` pins the old `ignoredDirs` deferral, so `validate:ci` and the spec's own `AC-NO-OTHER-FILES` cannot both pass. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-16 by the plan dispatch, drafting the plan against the ratified spec at `8348366` (base `5bf9723`), on a faithful whole-repository copy.** The spec's Constraints say "no `src/` file" and its `AC-NO-OTHER-FILES` asserts "`src/` is byte-identical". `src/grace-lint.test.ts:1930` — `it("keeps scripts in ignoredDirs")` — reads the repository's `.ngrace-lint.json` and asserts `ignoredDirs` **contains** `scripts`. Executing the spec's own deliverable (removing `"scripts"` from `ignoredDirs`) makes that assertion false, and there is no satisfying state: with the deliverable applied, `bun run validate:ci` exits **1** on that one test (`AC-SHAPE-CODE-SPLIT > keeps scripts in ignoredDirs`; 1970 pass, 1 fail, 3 skip) while the spec's `AC-NO-OTHER-FILES` `git diff --exit-code 5bf9723 …` on `src/` is green; flipping the assertion to `not.toContain("scripts")` takes `validate:ci` to **0** and reddens `AC-NO-OTHER-FILES` on `src/grace-lint.test.ts` (the diff is exactly that one file). Every other close-time command is green in the copy: the six `CloseEvidence` criteria recorded `Exit 0 / Result pass` after the close's `moved 2`, the adoption guard is 43 pass, and root lint with `scripts/` un-ignored is 0/0.
**The rule.** Every file the deliverable forces is in the spec's write scope, and every file the plan writes is excluded by the spec's byte-invariance criterion. The plan cannot repair this: `ngrace-plan` `must_do` 6 requires listing the forced `src/grace-lint.test.ts` in `ObservedWriteScope`, while the immutable `AC-NO-OTHER-FILES` command excludes no `src/` path. Owner: the maintainer's supersede of the approved spec (add `src/grace-lint.test.ts` to the write scope and to `AC-NO-OTHER-FILES`'s excludes), or the next `C-*` that adopts `scripts/`. The plan `C-SCRIPTS-ADOPTION-1-F621B7C0` is authored at `status="draft"` and must not be approved ahead of that supersede.

Finding.Title: ### F207 — the record has no schema: its shape and depth are convention, and nothing verifies them. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-09** at `b62698e`, when the authority claimed the record's depth was "fixed by schema" and the maintainer asked whether the schema is verified every time. It is not.
**What is checked:** XML well-formedness (`XMLValidator`, `parseGraceXmlArtifact`), targeted reads of named children (`childNodes(root, "Row")`, `"Decision"`, `"Finding"`, `"CodifiedIn"`, `"TaughtIn"`), root size attributes, and citation resolution.
**What is not checked, searched rather than assumed:** `grep` for `allowedChildren`, `requiredChildren` and `schema` across `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` and `scripts/prove-record-preservation.ts` returns **nothing**, and the record files appear nowhere in `src/artifact/grammar.ts` or `src/lint/catalog.ts`. The record is deliberately outside the artifact grammar — `C-RECORD-TEST-ISOLATION-2`'s spec forbids adding it — so **no rule constrains which children an element may have, how deep it may nest, or which are required.**
**So the observed depth 3 is an artefact of every writer happening to agree.** A record with a `Finding` nested inside a `Finding`, or an unexpected child, is well-formed and passes every shipped check.
**The consequence is not aesthetic.** `childNodes` reads **direct** children only, so a misplaced element is invisible to every structural count while still occupying lines. Under today's line metric it inflates the budget; under a structural metric it would vanish from it. **Any move to structural measurement ([F206](#f206)) must therefore ship a shape check first, or the new metric counts something undefined.**
Owner: a later bundle, and a prerequisite of the structural-metric charter rather than an independent nicety.

Finding.Title: ### F221 — byte-identity is not a holdable contract on a document nothing serializes canonically. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured **2026-09-10** at `299fc5c`, while verifying `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY`'s delivery.
The record is written by at least three paths that treat surrounding whitespace differently: the flush render, `persistSnapshot`'s root-line splice, and `--retire`'s element moves, whose span cut starts at the `<` and so does not carry a close tag's leading indent. Delivery drifted `</Findings>` from eight spaces to zero and `</Registry>` from thirty to thirty-two. Both files still parse; no element, attribute or text node moved.
**This is [F204](#f204)'s shape, and F204 blamed the wrong party.** There the drift came from `--retire` re-indenting structural lines and was recorded as bytes escaping a criterion's protection. The deeper fact is that **no writer canonicalizes**, so no two writers agree on whitespace, and a byte-level criterion is therefore a bet on which writer touched the file last.
**The remedy is a canonical serializer on every write, and the scalability argument settles it.** The alternative — preservation criteria that compare parsed trees instead of bytes — materializes both sides, and `parseGraceXmlArtifact` already buffers a whole document, so it costs O(2 x doc) on a record whose entire premise is unbounded growth. A canonical serializer is O(depth): read, normalize, emit. And once every writer routes through it, the identity check becomes a **hash** — streaming, constant memory, the cheapest check available rather than the most expensive.
A structural comparison could in principle stream too, two parsers walked in lockstep at O(depth). That does not rescue the alternative: it is more to build than a serializer, and it still only *detects* drift after it lands, where the serializer prevents it. The authority first recommended the tree comparison as "cheaper", meaning cheaper to implement, having never priced the runtime.
**Until the serializer lands, the standing rule:** a criterion asserting a file is unchanged says *structurally* unchanged and is answered by a parse, not by `git diff --exit-code`. Whitespace restored by hand to satisfy a byte check is a human doing a formatter's job, and it will drift again on the next write. The one-time cost the serializer carries is a single reflow of the record and the regeneration of every byte-pinned fixture; that is bounded, and the drift it removes is not.
Owner: a chartered bundle. Neighbour to [F204](#f204) (the symptom) and [F206](#f206) (a text metric over a structured document — the same category error, measured on volume instead of identity).

Finding.Title: ### F235 — a `--retire` pointed at a copied record directory from the repository's cwd reads the real archive, so a copy-drive of the close reports `moved 0` by construction. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-11 at `3f8a5ca`** by the executor revising `C-TAUGHT-RULES`'s spec, then re-driven by the authority. Eligibility keys on `<cwd>/.ngrace/changes/archive`: `listArchiveNames(repoRoot)` with `repoRoot = process.cwd()` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1843`-1863), while the record files are read from the directory argument. A drive that copies only `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH` and runs the move from the repository root therefore sees the copy's registry and the *real* archive: a row minted only in the copy, or a bundle archived only in the copy, is invisible, and the move reports `moved 0` — the spec's own `ExpectedCommand` carried exactly that form and could never have produced the `moved 5` it described. The faithful form copies the whole repository and runs the move from inside the copy (driven: `moved 5`).
**The class.** [F231](#f231) made the whole-repository copy the rule for `validate:ci`; this is the same rule for the record's own move, arrived at from the other side — the record-directory argument invites a partial copy that the engine silently half-honours. The remedy candidates: the engine takes the archive root from the record directory's own repository (walk up to `.ngrace/`), or refuses a record directory outside the cwd's repository. Either makes a partial copy loud.
Owner: the record-engine bundle that next touches `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`'s root resolution (the schema-and-serializer bundle `F207`/`F221` charter, or a payment-integrity bundle). Neighbour to [F231](#f231) and [F230](#f230).

Finding.Title: ### F252 — the flush projects the buffer's `---` separator into every non-last rendered `<Body>`: 54 of 319 record bodies end with a literal `---` line, and the buffer's own header tells the flusher to cut at that boundary first. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-14 at `18941b7`, the close of `C-PAIR-AUDIT-MINT-CWD-1-ED6B7D22`, by the authority's subagent and re-measured over the population.** Unescaping the rendered `<Body>` of `f250` and diffing it against its staged body shows one difference: a trailing blank line and a literal `---` that the staged entry does not carry — the section separator between it and `f251`. `f251`, the buffer's last entry, renders byte-identical. Over both findings layers (`perl -0777` over `<Finding …><Body>…</Body>`, 319 bodies), **54** end with a `---` line: `f8.1 … f242 f250` live and `f43 … f246 f247 f248` retired — every non-last entry of every flush since the split, so the shipped `parseFrozenMarkdown` returns `bodyRaw` with the separator and every flusher (`C-TEACH-DRIVE-BEFORE-APPROVE-2`'s included) rendered it through. The buffer header's own instruction — *"cut each body at the `---` or `## STAGED CHARTER` boundary first"* — is not what the parser does, and no walk asserts the body's tail.
**The rule.** The separator belongs to the buffer, never to a rendered body: `parseFrozenMarkdown` (or the render step) trims a trailing `---` and the blank line before it, a flush-invariant walk asserts no `<Body>` ends with a separator line, and the 54 existing bodies are cleaned in one sweep. Cosmetic in every consumer measured (nothing parses body tails), so it rides the next record-schema bundle (`F207`/`F221`) rather than its own. Owner: that bundle. **Re-measured 2026-09-16 at `aaae414` by parser over all four genre files: 68 bodies (findings 31 live + 23 retired; rulings 13 live + 1 retired) — the sweep covers every genre, and 56 of the 68 are attested by `record-inventory.json`, the split's preservation snapshot, whose hashes follow the sweep.**

Finding.Title: ### F265 — an approved spec carried "measured 0" for the golden fixtures' reflow, a figure taken over the live record and never over the fixtures; the golden relation test pins those bytes, and the copy drive at plan time found ten non-canonical gaps. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-16 at `a715692`** by the executor's plan-time copy drive and re-measured by the authority. The approved `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-1-1D8D868F` spec's write-scope Constraint listed `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/` as "regenerated only if the measured fixture diff is non-empty — measured 0", and its pin-grep Assumption stated that no test pins "a golden byte". Both were false when ratified: golden `rulings.xml` holds 5 of 61 `Decision`s at four-space indent and golden `rulings-retired.xml` holds all 5 at column zero (10 gap anomalies against the canonical form the spec defines), and `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2147` asserts a fixture `--retire` writes the golden files byte-for-byte. A serializer on every write therefore regenerates the goldens — the "regeneration of every byte-pinned fixture" that `F221` itself named as the serializer's one-time cost — and the approved spec had ruled the fixtures out of scope on a measurement of a different population.
**The class is [F130.1](#f130.1) and [F264](#f264) together.** The reflow was driven over the seven record files (0 bytes, true) and the result was written onto the fixtures (never driven); the pin grep looked for pins of root counts and indentation and did not open the one test whose title says "byte-for-byte". The authority's own verification drive covered the same seven files and not the goldens, and approved on it — the population a spec names is every file it names, fixtures included, and a figure attached to a file is a measurement of that file or it is not written.
**Remedy.** Superseded under D27 and the maintainer's V-A ruling (a stale figure in an approved spec is superseded, never carried): the successor states the fixtures' true state, puts the goldens in write scope as regenerated, names `:2147` as the pin the bundle flips, and pays this finding. Owner: `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2`.

Finding.Title: ### F266 — a per-test timeout is a ceiling that expires with the archive: the 111th archived bundle pushed two archive-walking review tests past the runner's 30 s, the fourth timeout incident in a week, and no fixed per-test number can hold on a corpus that grows by design. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-16** on CI run `35138369045` (branch `c-record-schema` at `844acd3`, the close of `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2-0785BD5E`): `src/review/core.test.ts`'s "archive corpus: zero live and retired findings on every dynamically enumerated C-*" (30 640 ms) and "archive ratchet: exact product multiset of three pairs" (31 353 ms) timed out under `bun test --timeout=30000`; locally the two take about 19 s together. Both enumerate every directory under `.ngrace/changes/archive/` (111 after the close), so their duration is linear in the corpus on a runner about three times slower than the development machine. The third archive walker in the run passed at 32 154 ms only because `C-STATUS-TEST-TIMEOUT-1-E7DA46E8` gave it `}, 60_000)` after the same failure shape (run `35017776037`); the next one sits at 25 976 ms. The tree carries 29 per-test pins across 5 files and three global values (`test` 30 s, `validate:cli` and `validate:determinism` 120 s), and `validate.yml` sets no `timeout-minutes` — the only real ceiling today is GitHub's six-hour default.
**The class.** A per-test timeout guards against a hung test, but every one of these pins was written to outrun the runner on a walk whose length is the archive, and the archive grows with every close. Each pin is therefore a dated measurement wearing a guard's clothes, and the incident recurs at the next threshold: four times this week. Bun honours `--timeout=0` as no per-test timeout (probed: a seven-second test passes under it and fails under the 5 s default), and the job-level `timeout-minutes` bounds a hang at the only scale that matters in CI.
**The remedy, the maintainer's ruling 2026-09-16 (variant B).** No per-test timeout: `--timeout=0` on every `bun test` invocation in `package.json`, every per-test pin removed (82 across six files once both syntactic forms are counted — the 29 above were the one-line form only), and one `timeout-minutes` on the CI job as the sole ceiling. This overturns `C-STATUS-TEST-TIMEOUT-1-E7DA46E8`'s per-test remedy and answers its argument: a walk over the real archive cannot carry a fixed number, so the guard moves to the job. Owner: a T0 bundle on the same branch, riding the same PR as the record-schema close (the #101 shape).

Finding.Title: ### F267 — a T0 spec that rewrites a skill sentence omitted the skill-footprint pin from its write scope and its byte-invariance criterion; the plan drive proved the criterion unsatisfiable, the third supersede of a bundle's own spec this week. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-16 at `e62ecf6`** by the executor's plan-time copy drive and re-driven by the authority. The approved `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-1-4985C820` spec rewrites one sentence of `skills/ngrace/ngrace-spec/SKILL.md` (and its packaged mirror), which moves the skill footprint `skillTextLines().totalBytes` from 78 384 to 78 456. That figure is pinned in `src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts:49` and in `README.md:304`; the plan skill's own row 6 says a skill-text change declares the skill-footprint pin, and every teaching bundle in the archive names `token-accounting.test.ts` in scope. The T0 spec named neither: its write-scope Constraint lists `README.md` for one line (`:382`) and its `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC` command excludes seventeen paths, not that test. On the post-close copy the criterion exits 1 naming exactly `src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts`, and `gate verdict` refuses `pass`. The spec's own tier Constraint lists "footprint Goals" among what T0 drops — the Goal is optional; the pin is a file the deliverable forces.
**The class is [F136](#f136) and [F265](#f265).** A scope contract that misses a file the deliverable forces cannot be satisfied by any plan, and the miss was in a place the authority had ruled to check (a pin grep before ratification — but for the *timeout* values, not for the skill bytes the same bundle moved). Third supersede of a bundle's own spec in one week ([F264](#f264), [F265](#f265), this): the pattern is a spec that changes one surface and is checked against that surface's pins only, while the change's second-order effect (a config's test pin, a fixture's bytes, a skill's footprint) sits in a file the spec never names. The pin grep must be run per *effect*, not per edited value.
**Remedy.** Superseded under D27: the successor names `src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts` in the write-scope Constraint and in `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC`'s excludes, states `README.md` carries two edits (`:304` and `:382`), and pays this finding with `F266`. Owner: `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-2`.

Finding.Title: ### F268 — `--assertions final --run-commands` re-opens an epoch and leaves a loose `command-run`, and `gate archive` refuses `gate.archive.open-epoch`; rule 7's note says "terminal and fold before gate archive" without saying *again, after final*. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `da727d0`** on a whole-repository copy (`rsync -a` of the working tree with a symlinked `node_modules`, `.ngrace/scratch` present, `active/` holding only `.gitkeep`). A throwaway bundle with an approved spec and plan (`C-PROBE-EPOCH-1-28D45FFA`, one `<MustPassCommand>true</MustPassCommand>`), driven through the close order:
- `cursor advance --change C-PROBE-EPOCH-1-28D45FFA --task T-001 --open-epoch` → epoch 1 open; `cursor advance --task T-001 --kind terminal`; `cursor fold` → `Epoch: 1 Events: 2`, `run/` empty. - `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --change C-PROBE-EPOCH-1-28D45FFA --assertions final --run-commands` → `Commands: 1 evaluated, 1 exit 0` (exit 1 on the throwaway's own lint errors), and `run/` now holds `3-T-001-command-run.xml` — final's `--run-commands` opened a fresh epoch and left a loose event. - `bun ./src/grace.ts gate archive --change C-PROBE-EPOCH-1-28D45FFA --path .` → `Decision: refuse`, `no-open-epoch: required=true present=false blocking=true — 1 loose run/ event(s)`, `[error] gate.archive.open-epoch`, exit 1. - second `cursor advance --task T-001 --kind terminal`; `cursor fold` (`Epoch: 2 Events: 3`) → `run/` empty; `gate archive` → `Decision: permit`, `no-open-epoch: required=true present=true blocking=false — run/ empty`, exit 0.
**The class.** Rule 7's note pins "*after a fold, final run-commands writes loose events and archive requires no-open-epoch, so terminal the declared task and fold before gate archive*" (`scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts:146`). It constrains *fold after terminal* and *final not after the fold*, but it does not say the terminal+fold must be re-emitted **after** `--assertions final --run-commands`. An executor that reads "before gate archive" as satisfied by one terminal+fold before final refuses at the archive gate; re-emitting terminal and folding again is what folds final's loose events. Recurrence of the same class as [F179](#f179), one layer later.
**Proposed rule.** `ngrace-execute` `execution_rules` (rule 7), appended: "After `--assertions final --run-commands`, terminal the declared task and fold again before `gate archive`: final run-commands opens a fresh epoch and leaves loose events, and the archive gate refuses `gate.archive.open-epoch` until they are folded." Token: `fold again before`.
Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F269 — rule 9 forbids the implementing executor to invoke `ngrace gate verdict` with no carve-out for the copy drive that row 19 requires; two executors met the contradiction and resolved it by reading the rule as production-scoped. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `da727d0`, from the tree and the two executors' reports.** `skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md` rule 9 states verbatim: "*The implementing executor does not invoke `ngrace gate verdict`.*" `skills/ngrace/ngrace-plan/SKILL.md` `must_do` row 19 requires the opposite act on a copy: "*Also drive the spec's `CloseEvidence` commands and the full CI in a faithful post-close copy at plan time*" and "*On the post-close copy, `ngrace gate verdict --change C --outcome pass` … evaluates every `CloseEvidence` command through the shell*." The `ngrace-execute` copy drive does the same. Two executors disclosed the conflict in their `SKILL GAPS`: one wrote "*The skill's rule 9 says the implementing executor does not invoke ngrace gate verdict; the brief item 5 requires it on the copy as the CloseEvidence probe. Brief/spec (copy probe) won over the skill's literal (production-close) reading; no gate verdict ran on production*"; the other wrote "*rule 9 … with no carve-out for the row-19 / sentence-(5) copy-drive use of the verb as a CloseEvidence probe. The plan (and the brief) require exactly that on a copy; the rule as written would forbid the only product-path evidence the bundle teaches*." Each resolved it by brief-over-skill, not by the skill.
**The class.** A rule scoped to the production close reads as a global prohibition, so the only compliant executor either produces no copy-drive evidence or knowingly routes around the skill — the latter being the exact failure the teaching surface exists to prevent.
**Proposed rule.** `ngrace-execute` `execution_rules` (rule 9), appended: "The prohibition is scoped to the production bundle: a faithful throwaway copy may invoke `ngrace gate verdict` as the `CloseEvidence` probe, and such a verdict is never recorded on the production record." Token: `a faithful throwaway copy may invoke`.
Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F271 — `ngrace-spec` names `spec new --supersedes` and `ngrace supersede` but not how a successor's *bytes* come to be, so authoring one is rediscovered each time. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `da727d0` over the archive.** Four successors were minted this month, each from a superseded predecessor and each carrying a lineage paragraph in `Problem`: `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-2-7AD2A006` (from `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-1-4985C820`, predecessor id appears 2 times in the successor's `spec.xml`, successor id 11), `C-SCRIPTS-ADOPTION-2-36DEB1BD` (from `C-SCRIPTS-ADOPTION-1-F621B7C0`; 3 / 15), `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-2-0785BD5E` (from `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-1-1D8D868F`; 7 / 15), and `C-TEACH-PLAN-DRIVES-CORRECTIONS-2-1E59AEAA` (from `C-TEACH-PLAN-DRIVES-CORRECTIONS-1-14457871`; 6 / 18); each predecessor's `spec.xml` reads `status="superseded"`. Every successor's `Problem` opens with a measured lineage paragraph naming the predecessor, the supersede commit and the reason; the remaining predecessor-id occurrences are lineage citations. `ngrace-spec` `shape_sources` names the lineage *path* (`spec new --supersedes`, `ngrace supersede`) and stops there; the authoring method — carry the predecessor's approved bytes and apply a bounded diff — is in no skill.
**Proposed rule.** `ngrace-spec` `shape_sources`, appended: "To author a successor, carry the archived approved predecessor's bytes and apply a bounded diff — the id where it is data, the lineage paragraph in `Problem`, and the change that forced the supersede — then count the diff and report the predecessor-id occurrences that remain." Token: `bounded diff`.
Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F272 — a criterion that pins the byte total of an artifact the executor will write, or of a fixture regenerated later, is falsified by the executed artifact and forces a supersede; the criterion states the relation and the projected figure belongs in `Assumptions`. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `da727d0` from the closed bundles.** `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-2-7AD2A006`'s spec `Assumptions` carries the copy drive's **draft** sentence figure ("**866 lines / 78 456 bytes** … a projection of that draft, not of the sentence the executor will write") while its `AC-TAUGHT-RULE` states the criterion as a **relation**: "*`src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts`'s `total`/`totalBytes` assertions and `README.md:304`'s cell equal the footprint **measured at HEAD after the rewrite** … the relation, not a number, is the criterion*." Its plan therefore carries `bun run test` (which evaluates the relation through the shipped test) rather than the number, and moved the predecessor's pinned `MustContain` figures out of `TargetAssertions`. The counterexample is [F265](#f265): `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-1-1D8D868F`'s write-scope Constraint ruled the golden fixtures "regenerated only if the measured fixture diff is non-empty — measured 0", a figure taken over the live record and never over the fixtures; the plan-time drive found ten non-canonical goldens and the figure was already false at ratification.
**The class.** A number projected onto an artifact that does not exist yet at approval time is a dated measurement in a criterion's clothes: the executed artifact overwrites it, the pin reddens, and the repair is a supersede. The relation (`pin equals measurement`) is invariant under the executor's bytes.
**Proposed rule.** `ngrace-spec` `acceptance_criteria_anchors`, appended: "A criterion that pins an artifact the executor will write, or a fixture regenerated later, states the relation — the pin equals the measurement — and never the projected figure; the figure belongs in `Assumptions`, where it expires." Token: `states the relation`.
Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F273 — three supersedes in one week had one shape: the spec was checked against the pins of the value it edited while the change's second-order effect sat in a file the spec never named; the pin grep must be run per effect, before ratification. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `da727d0` over the retired record.** The bodies of [F264](#f264), [F265](#f265) and [F267](#f267) each describe the same failure: a spec that flips one value and is checked against that value's pins while a *different* file pins the consequence. `F264`: `C-SCRIPTS-ADOPTION-1-F621B7C0` forbade every `src/` write while `src/grace-lint.test.ts:1930` pins `ignoredDirs ∋ scripts`, so `validate:ci` and the spec's own `AC-NO-OTHER-FILES` could not both pass — superseded. `F265`: `C-RECORD-SCHEMA-1-1D8D868F` ruled the golden fixtures out of scope on "measured 0" while `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2147` pins the goldens byte-for-byte — superseded. `F267`: `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-1-4985C820` rewrote a skill sentence and omitted `src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts` and `README.md:304` from scope and criterion — superseded. The archive search is the wrong population for a second-order pin: it is the *test suites* that pin the consequence.
**Proposed rule.** `ngrace-spec` `acceptance_criteria_anchors`, appended: "Before ratification, list what the deliverable moves and grep the test suites for each — skill text moves the footprint pins, fixture inputs or engine output move golden bytes, config values move the audit and lint guards, the record moves the payer maps — and name every file the grep finds in the write scope." Token: `list what the deliverable moves`.
Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F274 — landing a later guard in an earlier pair's landing makes the earlier pair's whole-suite green impossible; the T0 executor reworked its first landing, and no rule says one guard per pair. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `da727d0` from the T0 bundle's report and ledger.** `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-2-7AD2A006`'s report `SKILL GAPS` records: "*ngrace-execute does not warn that a task's first red-first pair can be invalidated by landing a second guard the same task's later pair owns: the plan sequences pin-guard before ceiling-guard, but nothing tells the executor not to batch both into the first landing, and batching makes the first pass's whole-suite green impossible. A sentence in `must_do`/`assertion_commands` would have saved a rework of the first landing.*" Its `run-ledger.xml` shows the corrected shape after the rework: three separate pairs, `fail pin-guard` → `pass`, `fail ceiling-guard` → `pass`, `fail footprint-pin` → `pass` (events 7–12). `ngrace-execute` rule 5 governs the fix budget and rule 13 the pass-only cycle; neither says a guard lands with its own pair.
**Proposed rule.** `ngrace-execute` `execution_rules` (rule 5), appended: "Land one guard per pair: a guard a later pair owns, landed with the first pair's fix, is red until its own pair lands and makes the first pair's whole-suite green impossible — batch the fix, not the guards." Token: `one guard per pair`.
Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F275 — when a successor spec turns a pinned number into a relation, the archived plan's `TargetAssertions` that pinned the number must become the relation; `approved_plan_immutability` says re-home from the archived draft and nothing about this. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `da727d0` over the two archived plans.** `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-1-4985C820`'s `plan.xml` `TargetAssertions` pin the footprint as a number: `<MustContain><File>README.md</File><Text>**866 lines** / **78456 UTF-8 bytes**</Text></MustContain>` and `<MustContain><File>src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts</File><Text>expect(measured.totalBytes).toBe(78456);</Text></MustContain>`. The successor `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-2-7AD2A006` turned the criterion into a relation and its `TargetAssertions` carry `bun run test` (the shipped test evaluates the relation) and no footprint number. `ngrace-plan` `approved_plan_immutability` says to author the successor's artifacts from the archived predecessor's draft, changing the id where it is data; it does not say that a criterion which changed *kind* — number to relation — must be re-homed in `TargetAssertions`, not carried.
**Proposed rule.** `ngrace-plan` `approved_plan_immutability`, appended: "When the successor's spec turns a pinned number into a relation, re-home the archived plan's `TargetAssertions` the same way: the pinned number becomes the relation, never a figure carried across the supersede." Token: `the pinned number becomes the relation`.
Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F276 — a tier drops Goals, never a forced file: the T0 that dropped the footprint Goal also dropped the footprint pin from write scope, and the bundle was uncloseable. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `da727d0` from [F267](#f267)'s body and the predecessor spec.** The T0 tier table in `ngrace-spec` `ceremony_tiers` says T0 shrinks `Summary`/`Problem`, narrows `AffectedAreas` and keeps "minimal `AcceptanceCriteria`", and the T0 spec's own tier Constraint listed "footprint Goals" among what T0 drops. `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-1-4985C820` dropped the footprint *Goal* and, with it, `src/test-support/token-accounting.test.ts` and `README.md:304` from the write-scope Constraint and the byte-invariance criterion; on the post-close copy the criterion exited 1 naming that test and `gate verdict` refused `pass` — superseded as `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-2-7AD2A006`. The Goal is optional at T0; the file the deliverable forces is not, because without it the bundle cannot close.
**Proposed rule.** `ngrace-spec` `ceremony_tiers`, appended: "A tier changes which sections must be rich, never which files are in scope: T0 may drop a Goal, but a file the deliverable forces stays in the write scope, or the bundle is uncloseable." Token: `never which files are in scope`.
Owner: the next teaching increment.

Finding.Title: ### F228 — a duplicate live finding id crashes `--retire` before any write, with a message that names the wrong cause. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
Measured by the executor during `C-ROOT-WINDOW`'s probes, 2026-09-11: a `Finding` whose `id` already names an index `Entry` that an earlier item of the same move spliced — a duplicate live id, which the record shape check does not forbid — makes `--retire` throw in `setEntryLayer` with *"no readable layer attribute"*. The throw is before any write, so the record is not corrupted; the message blames the attribute when the cause is the duplicate. Loud-before-write is the right behaviour; the diagnosis is the defect. The shape check's silence on duplicate ids is the same gap [F207](#f207) records from the schema side.
Owner: a later bundle on the engine surface, sized by the authority. Neighbour to [F207](#f207).

Finding.Title: ### F277 — the validator accepts an index `Entry` whose `layer` disagrees with the file holding its genre element, so a hand edit moves an index line to the retired layer without moving the entry and relieves the index budget while the record stays green. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `5d9a5c89a4b6e57999051e169c89d36570e4081d`.** On a whole-record copy, flipping one live finding's index line from `layer="live"` to `layer="retired"` (`<Entry id="f1" token="F1" genre="finding" layer="live" />` → `... layer="retired" />`), leaving `findings.xml` untouched, is accepted by `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts .ngrace/tmp-record2` (`record-retirement: ok`, exit 0, stderr empty) while the unmodified control copy is equally `ok`. `--rewrite-roots` then reads the index's shipped metric back — `liveEntryCount` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:995`), the index genre's metric in `rewriteRecordRoots` (`:1325`) — and persists `base="264" headroom="32" ceiling="296"` against the control's `base="265" headroom="31" ceiling="296"`: the flip relieves the index budget by one live entry while the entry itself is unmoved, and the ceiling holds. Nothing compares an `Entry`'s `layer` to the holding genre element: `checkStatusFile` (`:1610`) runs for `Finding`/`Decision`/`Row` only and never for `Entry`; `recordSchemaViolations` (`scripts/record-serialize.ts:157`) is per-element and per-file; `validate-citation-anchors.ts:124` checks index id-duplication and the inventory↔index relation but not `layer`; `prove-record-preservation.ts` checks the inventory id/token relation and body hashes, not `layer`. The shipped per-bundle "exists exactly once across the layers with its index `Entry` layer agreeing" walks cover only the ids each flush names, so the record's older ids are unprotected and a layer flip on any of them is silent.
**Proposed owner.** The engine surface that already owns the pair invariants. The same bundle that pays `F228` (the validator's silence on duplicate ids, one invariant over) can extend the shared structural check to "every index `Entry`'s `layer` equals the layer of the file holding its genre element, for every id across both genre pairs", as a named validator finding, a `--retire` refusal, and a `--flush` refusal. Sized by the authority. Neighbour to `F228` (same validator-silence class) and `F221` (structural drift nothing canonicalizes).

Finding.Title: ### F278 — an approved spec had the flush verb write a decision's resolving `CodifiedIn` mid-execution, against the shipped one-wave rule that the close writes the element and moves it together; the plan could only comply by taking the record validator off the task boundary. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `5de3373`** by the executor's plan drive and re-read by the authority. The approved `C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-1-464041EE` spec's dogfood Goal has the first verb flush write `F277`, the charter row **and `D40`'s `CodifiedIn`** in one invocation during execution. A resolving `CodifiedIn` makes a live decision eligible at once: the validator reports `decision-eligible-still-live` and `validate:ci` reds on the production tree from that task until the close's `--retire`. The rule that forbids this is shipped and archived — `C-APPLY-VERB`'s plan: *"Do not write CodifiedIn on D37 (after a resolving CodifiedIn a live Decision is immediately decision-eligible; decision-eligible-still-live fails a task boundary that holds that tree; the close writes the element and --retire in one wave)"* — and D37's `CodifiedIn` was written in the close commit (`17d8b47`). The draft plan complied by excluding the record suite and the validator from `TargetAssertions` and from two tasks' `Verification`: an instrument routed around a boundary it exists to guard.
**The class.** A spec named a mechanism (`--codify`) without reading the ruling that fixes its *timing* — rule 9's "find the decision that created the behaviour" applied to a close act. Same shape as [F273](#f273)'s: the change's second-order effect (a record state the validator refuses) sat in a place the spec never looked, here an archived plan's task note rather than a test pin. The authority approved it with the same gap.
**Remedy.** Superseded under D27: the successor's execution flush writes the findings and the row only; the verb gains a codify-only invocation (no entries, the existing row recognised, one `CodifiedIn` written through the same transaction) that the **authority runs at the close** with the bundle still active, immediately followed by `apply` and `--retire` — the one-wave rule kept, and the write still the verb's (D40). Owner: `C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2`.

Finding.Title: ### F279 — a shipped test sourced its fixture from a path git does not track, so the suite is green in the maintainer's working tree and red in every clone; a close can sign off on evidence CI disproves. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `0044fbe1ef4aaadf9bfd38be0fef90e4a41a51cb`.** `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:6232`, inside the `C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A flush mode` describe (`:6221`), builds its fixture with `plant(root, ".ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md", readFileSync(path.join(REPO_ROOT, ".ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md"), "utf8"))` — the live authority buffer, planted into an isolated root. The path is `.gitignore`d (`.gitignore:8`, `.ngrace/scratch/`) and tracked by nothing, so it exists in the maintainer's tree and in no clone. Two runs at the same commit, `bun test --timeout=0` with the exit read directly (`> log 2>&1; echo EXIT=$?`): in a fresh `git clone` of this branch plus `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, **2009 pass, 3 fail, 3 skip** (EXIT=1), all three failures in that describe, each carrying `error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '<clone>/.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md'` at `flushRoot (scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:6232:55)`; in this working tree, **2012 pass, 0 fail, 3 skip** (EXIT=0). The delta is exactly the three tests the buffer read feeds. The archived Constraint that pointed the fixture at that path is `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RECORD-FLUSH-VERB-2-6BB9DF5A/spec.xml:323` ("`.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` is **read, never written**") with `:341` staging new findings there.
**The population, measured.** Across **64** `*.test.ts` files (the whole set: `find . -name '*.test.ts' -not -path './node_modules/*'`), exactly **one** read names a `.gitignore`d or untracked repository path — that line (`grep -rn "\.ngrace/scratch" --include='*.test.ts'` returns one hit; `grep -rn "node_modules\|\.claude\|DS_Store" --include='*.test.ts'` returns none). Non-test code under `src/` and `scripts/`: **none** reads an ignored or untracked path; the six hits on `node_modules` are `src/project-utils.ts:102` (`DEFAULT_IGNORED_DIRS`, a skip list), `src/review/core.ts:396` and `:461` (skip filters on a user's tree) and `:432` (a comment), `scripts/validate-marketplace.ts:161` (a skip filter) and `scripts/packed-cli-smoke.ts:155` (a temp consumer's own `node_modules`, created by the script). A shipped guard that would have caught the test: **none exists** — `git check-ignore`, `git ls-files`, `git worktree`, `git archive` and `git clone` appear in no `src/`, `scripts/` or workflow file, and `.gitignore` is named in none (searched every form; the only `git status --untracked-files=all` use is the review engine deriving changed files, `src/review/core.ts:2009`, and `scripts/skill-contracts.test.ts:207` asserts a skill string). CI's fresh `actions/checkout` in `.github/workflows/validate.yml:16,41,68` is the state the working tree diverges from, and nothing in the repository compares the two.
**The class.** A shipped test whose fixture is sourced from a path git does not track is green only where that path exists — the maintainer's tree. `bun run validate:ci` run there therefore does not predict CI: the bundle's own `CloseEvidence` (`bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, the archived spec's `AC-FLUSH-MODE`) was green locally for a reason the runner cannot reproduce, and the close signed off on evidence CI disproves. The dependency is on session state as well as a missing file: the buffer's header rule prunes entries after their PR merges, so the fixture's content changes under the test even where the file exists.
**Remedy.** The fixture becomes self-contained in the test file (a literal buffer, independent of the record's state and the buffer's contents), and a shipped guard in the shape of `C-TEST-TIMEOUT-CEILING-2-7AD2A006`'s suite-hygiene test fails when any `.ts` file passes a path git does not track to a filesystem read — keyed on read call sites, so `src/review/core.ts`'s mention of `node_modules` is not a false positive. Owner: `C-CLONE-FAITHFUL-TESTS-1-D68520A2`.

Finding.Title: ### F281 — the suite's wall clock is dominated by O(n²) re-derivation of the immutable archive: `readAmendmentInstrument` rebuilds a 117-bundle predecessor map once per change, and `validate:ci` re-runs whole test files the full suite just ran. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `2434fd4` (branch `c-test-time-budget`, bun 1.4.2, macOS arm64).** Every count below is reproducible from one `bun test --timeout=0 --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=…` over the tree; per-test durations are parsed from that JUnit file, not sampled.
**The population.** 2017 tests across 64 files, 138.83 s wall (`Ran 2017 tests across 64 files. [138.83s]`, exit 0). Testcase time sums to 138.62 s. 22 tests are ≥1.0 s and together are 72.92 s (52.6% of the suite); 41 are ≥0.5 s (86.76 s); 1701 are <0.05 s and together are 4.38 s. Per-file totals, top seven: `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` 42.14 s / 163 tests; `src/review/core.test.ts` 23.76 s / 188; `src/grace-context.test.ts` 19.59 s / 30; `src/gates/core.test.ts` 14.67 s / 111; `src/grace-status.test.ts` 13.41 s / 55; `src/grace-query.test.ts` 5.93 s / 42; `src/grace-lint.test.ts` 4.32 s / 114. Those seven files are 123.82 s of 138.62 s (89.3%).
**The slowest tests, named.** `src/grace-status.test.ts:1131` "live repo reports measured reRatificationCount table…" 11.21 s; `src/review/core.test.ts:2456` "archive ratchet: exact product multiset of three pairs…" 10.76 s; `src/review/core.test.ts:1982` "archive corpus: zero live and retired findings on every dynamically enumerated C-*" 10.57 s; `src/grace-context.test.ts:522` "measures three named archive tasks…" 9.03 s; `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1939` "C-RECORD-PARSE equivalence class…" 3.80 s; `src/grace-context.test.ts:561` 2.96 s; `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:6305` 2.26 s; `src/grace-context.test.ts:491` 2.04 s; `src/grace-query.test.ts:870` 2.03 s.
**Passes per CI run.** `package.json:79` chains `bun run typecheck && bun run test && … && bun run validate:cli && … && bun run validate:determinism && …`. Each is a separate process: `test` = `bun test --timeout=0` (`:67`, the full 64-file/2017-test suite); `validate:cli` = `bun test --timeout=0 src/grace-lint.test.ts src/grace-status.test.ts src/grace-query.test.ts` (`:69`), 211 tests / 25.02 s, all already run by `test`; `validate:determinism` = `bun test --timeout=0 src/review/core.test.ts src/review/scorer.test.ts && …` (`:71`), 196 tests / 24.36 s, all already run by `test`. So one `bun run validate:ci` executes **2424 test runs for 2017 distinct tests** — 407 duplicate executions costing **49.38 s** of the run. `.github/workflows/validate.yml:30` then runs `bun run validate:determinism` a **third** time (196 more executions, 24.36 s) after `validate:ci` already ran it at `:71`. The full-suite wall of `validate:ci` is 138.83 + 25.02 + 24.36 = **188.21 s**, of which 49.38 s (26%) re-runs work the full suite completed moments earlier; CI re-runs 603 tests (24% of executions) that a single pass would cover.
**Where the wall clock goes — not process startup, not file reads; O(n²) re-derivation.** `bun ./src/grace.ts --version` starts in **0.09 s**; reading every archived `spec.xml`/`plan.xml` twice (11.07 MB across 117 bundles) takes **7.6 ms**; reading all seven record XML files twice (1.13 MB) takes **0.7 ms**. The cost is CPU re-derivation. `collectProjectStatus(REPO_ROOT)` (`src/grace-status.ts:373`) is **11.73 s** on this tree. Of that, `collectChangeBundleStatuses` (`src/grace-status.ts:165`) calls `readAmendmentInstrument(root, changeId)` (`src/grace-status.ts:228`) once per bundle; `readAmendmentInstrument` (`src/gates/ledger.ts:1187`) calls `buildPredecessorMap(projectRoot)` (`src/gates/ledger.ts:1191`), and `buildPredecessorMap` (`src/gates/ledger.ts:1134`) reads every bundle via `listChangeBundleDirs`/`replacementIdsForBundle` (`:1119`, `:1113`). Measured: `readAmendmentInstrument` ×1 = **115.4 ms**, ×117 = **9.94 s** — 117 rebuilds of the same immutable map, ~117 × 117 = 13 689 bundle reads. `src/review/core.ts:1717` calls the same `readAmendmentInstrument` inside every `runReview` with `processAudits` on: `runReview(repoRoot, {changeId, changedFiles: [], patterns: false, joinEngine: false})` is **114.6 ms** per call and **0.0 ms** with `processAudits: false`; ×117 (the archive loop at `src/review/core.test.ts:1995` and `:2483`) = **10.33 s** per test, twice. Separately, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:50` spawns `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` via `runValidator` for 163 tests; that file is 42.14 s, ~258 ms per spawn.
**Local versus runner.** 138.83 s locally. The inherited runner figure (232 s against ~137–141 s locally, ~1.7×) is **not re-driven here** — this dispatch has no CI runner. The pinned job ceiling is `timeout-minutes: 30` (`.github/workflows/validate.yml:12`).
**The memo payoff, re-driven 2026-09-17 on a throwaway `git worktree` at `2434fd4` (not inherited).** A prototype memoizing `buildPredecessorMap` per resolved root, keyed on the sorted `(bundle name, spec/plan size, mtimeMs)` revision, took `src/review/core.test.ts` **23.44 s → 3.03 s** and `src/grace-status.test.ts` **13.92 s → 3.83 s**, 0 failures each, and the full suite **138.83 s → 109.64 s** (`Ran 2017 tests across 64 files. [109.64s]`, exit 0). One memo alone is ~29 s off the suite.
**The frequency half is teaching, and this bundle pays both.** The memoization above removes ~29 s from one suite run, but the maintainer's stated pain is that a single turn runs the full verification several times over — and that multiplicity is mandated by skill text, not by test speed. Measured from the archived `C-CLONE-FAITHFUL-TESTS-1-D68520A2` bundle (parsed 2026-09-17 at `2434fd4`): one close ran the full suite or its CI equivalent **six times** — T-001 `bun run test`, T-002 `bun run validate:ci`, `TargetAssertions` `MustPassCommand` `bun run validate:ci` at `--assertions target`, the same at `--assertions final`, the `AC-*` `CloseEvidence` `bun run test`, and the authority's close `validate:ci` — plus repeated subset runs (`bun run typecheck` ×3, `bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` ×3, `bun test scripts/audit-regressions.test.ts` ×2). At ~140 s that is ~17 minutes of suite time per bundle. A search of `skills/ngrace/*/SKILL.md` for frequency-limiting language (`full suite`, `whole suite`, `exactly once`, `only once`, `once per`, `per-task`) finds no passage that caps how often the full verification runs; the `ngrace-plan` `must_do` row 12 only requires non-empty per-task verification, and `ngrace-execute` rule 7 runs `--assertions final --run-commands`. So the frequency defect is a teaching gap: no skill sentence can memoize a function (**Goal 2's half**), and no memo can teach a turn to stop re-running the whole suite (**the frequency half**). This bundle pays both, and its remedy set is the six Goals of `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-1-98736D59`.
**Proposed owner.** This bundle, `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET`, ceremony tier **T3** (the change reaches the taught lifecycle contract across `ngrace-spec`, `ngrace-plan` and `ngrace-execute`, both skill trees, the taught-rule token tables, the skill-footprint pins and `README.md`): memoize the immutable per-root corpus derivations (`buildPredecessorMap` first); collapse the duplicated suite passes in `validate:ci` and the workflow; add a non-gating selective developer-loop runner; keep per-test metrics current; move the bulk of the 163 validator spawns in-process where the contract under test is not the process boundary; and teach the verification-frequency rule so the full CI-equivalent run happens **once per turn** rather than three or four times.
Owner: this bundle (`C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET`); this entry is the measurement it pays.

Finding.Title: ### F282 — an approved spec forced edits to two files it did not scope, because the scope check anchored the files the deliverable *names* and never the guards that assert what the deliverable *removes*. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `b9b45f3`,** at the plan stage of `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-1-98736D59`, by driving the guards rather than reading them. The spec's Goal 1(a) removes `bun run validate:cli` from both `validate:ci` and `validate:release`. Two shipped guards assert that `validate:release` *must* invoke it: `scripts/validate-marketplace.ts:336`–`338` (`errors.push("package.json: validate:release must invoke validate:cli")`) and `scripts/release-checklist.ts:250` (`ok: Boolean(packageJson.scripts?.["validate:release"]?.includes("validate:cli") && …)`). Neither file appears in the spec's write-scope `Constraint`, and neither is among the four `scripts/*.ts` non-test paths excluded by `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC`. Because `bun run ./scripts/validate-marketplace.ts` is itself a member of `validate:ci`, the deliverable reddens CI the moment it lands, and the bundle is uncloseable as approved — the same shape as [F136](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) and [F267](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md).
**The generalisable half — the rule the existing checks do not carry.** The authority's standing scope check reads each file the spec's `Constraints` *name* and confirms its owning module appears in every module list. That check passed here: `M-GATES` and `M-SKILLS` were both anchored, and `src/gates/ledger.ts:5` carries its `LINKS:` header. It passed and the spec was still uncloseable, because a deliverable that **removes** a value forces every guard that **asserts** that value, and those guards are named nowhere in the spec. **The missing step: for each value the deliverable deletes, moves or renames, grep the tree for the assertions of that value and scope what the grep finds.** `grep -rn '"validate:release"' scripts/ src/ --include='*.ts'` returns both guards in one command, and was never run before approval.
**Why the remedy is narrowing, not widening.** Adding both guards to scope would edit a deliberate release-safety check so that it permits what it exists to forbid, and buys nothing: `validate:release` runs at release time, never inside a development turn, so removing its `validate:cli` saves no turn time. No guard constrains `validate:ci`'s composition (`scripts/release-checklist.ts:245` only asserts the script exists), so confining Goal 1(a) to `validate:ci` keeps the entire measured saving, leaves both guards green, and forces no new file into scope. Recorded under [D11](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md): the successor shrinks the goal rather than deferring it.
Owner: paid by the successor of `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-1-98736D59`, whose bounded diff narrows Goal 1(a) and `AC-FEWER-PASSES` to `validate:ci`.

Finding.Title: ### F286 — the archive-corpus attempt-pair invariant holds a **superseded** bundle's abandoned run stream to the corroboration standard, so any bundle superseded after partial execution permanently reds the whole suite. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `423adf9`,** by the authority, on a clean tree. `bun test src/review/core.test.ts` exits 1 with one failure: `attempt-pair identical-tree (C-SUBSTANTIATION-HONESTY) > archive corpus: zero live and retired findings on every dynamically enumerated C-*`. The test (`src/review/core.test.ts:1985`–`2010`) enumerates every directory under `.ngrace/changes/archive/` whose name starts with `C-`, runs `runReview` against each, and asserts `expect(live).toHaveLength(0)` and `expect(retired).toHaveLength(0)` for the attempt-pair codes. `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016` now sits in that corpus carrying the two uncorroborated `fail→pass` pairs recorded in [F283](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md), so the sum is 2 and `bun run validate:ci` exits 1.
**The invariant is correct and the cause is not the supersede.** The guard exists to refuse an uncorroborated pair entry into the permanent archive, and it is doing exactly that. `F283`'s two mis-ordered events made that bundle **unarchivable by any route**: a normal close moves the bundle into `archive/` with `ngrace apply`, so the post-close `validate:ci` would have reddened identically. Driven both ways: at `68ec888`, with the bundle still under `active/`, the same guard is 1 pass / 0 fail, exit 0; at `423adf9`, with it archived, 0 pass / 1 fail, exit 1. The archive move is the trigger, not the verb that performed it.
**The design flaw the episode exposes.** `ngrace supersede` "discards governance, never code" — a superseded bundle's run stream is abandoned governance, not delivered evidence. The audit draws no such distinction: it walks every archived `C-*` regardless of whether its spec and plan read `applied`, `superseded`, `rejected` or `cancelled`. The consequence generalises well beyond this bundle: **any bundle superseded after partial execution, carrying any imperfect attempt pair, reds the entire suite permanently**, because `archive/` is immutable and the pairs cannot be repaired. A methodology that mandates supersede as the only repair for an approved artifact cannot also make mid-execution supersede a permanent red.
**The shape of the remedy, not the remedy itself.** Either exempt bundles whose spec status is terminal-but-not-`applied` from the attempt-pair archive walk, or enumerate only `applied` bundles. There is adjacent precedent for treating archived governance more leniently — `src/lint/core.ts:544` holds archived plans to "syntax only, never semantic (baseline may be stale, target may be superseded by later changes)" — so the exemption is a consistent extension rather than a new principle, but it is still a product-behaviour change to `src/review/core.ts` and its guard, and it needs an authorizing spec that says which ruling it extends.
**Why it cannot be repaired inside the bundle that found it.** `src/review/core.ts` and `src/review/core.test.ts` appear in neither `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-3-7950A760`'s write-scope `Constraint` nor `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC`'s exclude pathspec, so editing either reddens a close-bound criterion — the [F136](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md)/[F282](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md)/[F285](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) shape a fourth time. Only one active bundle is permitted (`ngrace-execute` `<preflight>`), so a separate bundle cannot run alongside, and after it landed it would redden `C-3`'s byte-invariance criterion anyway.
Owner: the successor of `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-3-7950A760`, which scopes the audit change alongside the landed test-time work.

Finding.Title: ### F289 — the flush verb's `--decision` path writes an index `Entry` but never the `Decision` element, so a flushed decision leaves the record pointing at nothing. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `82aa877`,** by the authority, driving the shipped verb against the production record during the close of `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E`. The invocation `bun ./scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts --flush … --finding F281 --finding F282 --finding F286 --decision D41 --pays "F281 F282 F286" …` exited **0** and printed `record-flush: flushed F281 F282 F286 D41 (row …, pays F281 F282 F286)` — naming `D41` as flushed. The record disagreed: `grep -c d41` over `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` returned **0** each, `rulings.xml`'s live root was byte-unchanged at `base="1670" headroom="213" ceiling="1883"`, and `git diff --stat` over the record showed three files touched — `decisions.xml`, `findings.xml`, `registry.xml` — with `rulings.xml` absent. Meanwhile `decisions.xml` carried `<Entry id="d41" token="D41" genre="decision" layer="live" />`: an index line asserting a live decision that exists in no genre file.
**The cause, read from the engine.** In `flushRecord` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`), `nextFindings` appends `selF` to `findings.xml` and `nextIndex` appends index entries for **both** `selF` and `selD`, but `nextRulings` is initialised to the unchanged `rulingsXml` and is rewritten **only** inside `if (opts.codify)`. There is no path that appends a selected decision's element. `--decision` therefore mints an orphan index row on every invocation that uses it, and the printed confirmation names the token as flushed.
**Why the schema did not catch it.** The refusals that run before the write check duplicate ids across the genre pair, an existing row, `--pays` tokens, charter and status-text prose, and `mint-search` shape; none asserts that a selected decision appears in the next `rulings.xml`. `assertRecordSchema` validates each next-document in isolation, so an index with a row and a rulings file without the element are each well-formed on their own. This is the index-versus-genre disagreement `F277` names, reached through the shipped write path rather than a hand edit — and the layer agrees, so `F277`'s own check would not fire either.
**Recovery, and the shape it should have.** The authority reverted the record through git (the flush was uncommitted), then re-ran the same flush without `--decision`; the three findings and the row landed correctly and `d41` appears nowhere. `D41` stays staged in the buffer until the verb can carry it. Note the asymmetry the recovery depended on: had the flush been committed, the only repair would have been a hand edit of the record, which `D41` itself forbids.
Owner: a record-engine bundle — `--decision` either appends the element and the index entry together, or refuses with a named code. Stays staged, together with `D41`, which cannot be flushed until then.

Finding.Title: ### F288 — two concurrent `ngrace cursor advance` invocations mint the **same** event id (no lock or reservation), and the duplicate ids make `cursor fold` refuse with "payload mismatch", leaving the bundle unarchivable. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 during `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-4-F173437E`** (HEAD `4d497ae` plus the uncommitted T-009/T-010 writes; bun 1.4.2). Recording the execution's structural events, two `ngrace cursor advance` progress calls for `T-002` and `T-003` were issued in one tool round trip; **both wrote `run/` files carrying `id="5"`** (`5-T-002-progress.xml`, `5-T-003-progress.xml`). The same collision hit `T-004`/`T-005` (`id="8"`) and `T-006`/`T-007` (`id="11"`). Every attempt event kept a unique id; only the concurrently-issued progress events collided.
**The cause, read not inferred.** `nextEventId` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:3337`) reads `listLooseEvents(bundlePath)`, takes `looseMax`, and returns `Math.max(floor, looseMax + 1, ledgerMax + 1)`; `writeEventFile` then writes the new file. Read → compute → write with **no lock and no reservation**, so two processes that read the same `looseMax` both mint the same id. `listLooseEvents` names files `<id>-<task>-<kind>.xml` (`EVENT_FILENAME`, `src/artifact/run-membership.ts:48`), and the collision is silent — both invocations exit 0. `nextEventId` is called from **eight** sites in `src/grace-cursor.ts` (`:753` covering opened, `:978` `openEpoch`, `:1084` `advance`, `:1340` discard, `:2005`/`:2033` `recordAttempt` and its circuit trip, `:2116` verification-unavailable, `:3267` command-run), not four: every append path shares the defect. Because the task and kind are in the filename, the same id splits two ways — different task/kind leaves two files with duplicate ids, the same task/kind **overwrites one file with the other**.
**The consequence, driven on a copy.** `ngrace cursor fold` on the bundle (a `git worktree` copy of the production `run/` plus a terminal event) **exits 1**: `Fold verify failed: event 5 payload mismatch (attributes or children dropped or altered).` `foldEpoch` (`:1143`) verifies every ledger `Event` against the loose event of the same id, and two loose events share id 5. Because `gate archive` refuses an open epoch and `ngrace-execute` rule 7 requires terminal + fold before archive, a collision like this makes the bundle **uncloseable** without a repair.
**The second symptom and the misdiagnosis, re-driven 2026-09-17 at `b6d7aba` on a throwaway `/tmp/race` project (bun 1.4.2).** Twelve concurrent `cursor advance` calls with twelve distinct tasks, after one `--open-epoch --from 1 --to 199`, produced **13 files with 5–6 distinct ids in all ten rounds**; twelve concurrent calls on the **same** task `T-001` left only **3–4 files**, so 8–9 events were lost with every invocation exiting 0 — silent evidence loss, a second and worse half of this defect that the original incident did not show. On the collided stream `ngrace cursor recover` exits **0** and prints **`Fold: ok`**, because `validateEventsAgainstAllocations` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:2810`) tests range membership, `range hole` density and the closer over a `Set` of ids and never reads a duplicate; `cursor fold` refuses with `payload mismatch`, which names a lost payload rather than a duplicated id; `cursor regenerate` (dry-run) and `cursor show` both exit 0 without a finding. `ngrace supersede` refuses the same stream with the identical fold error, because `supersedeChangeBundle` (`src/gates/ledger.ts:1519`) calls `discardAndFoldEpoch` before it writes `superseded`.
**The repair, disclosed.** The three duplicate progress events were renumbered — filename and `id` attribute, to 21/22/23, every event's content otherwise preserved. On a fresh copy the fold then exits 0 (`Fold applied … Events: 24`); the production `run/` now holds 24 unique ids. No shipped verb performs this repair: `cursor regenerate` (dry-run) does not report the collision, `cursor recover --fix` only extends covering allocations, and `cursor recover` affirmatively prints `Fold: ok`. Hand-editing the run stream was the only available route and is not a sanctioned one — which is the point of this entry.
**Why it is not just a usage error.** `--parallel-preflight` exists and `ngrace-execute`'s `mode_selection` admits parallel-safe batches, so concurrent cursor invocation is a shape the product invites; even outside that, nothing in the CLI warns, locks, or refuses. A collision either silently corrupts the stream (as here) or, if a later event reuses the id, would alias two events for the attempt-pair audit as well. The record already carries cursor-integrity entries; none names id allocation. Grep for `nextEventId`, `duplicate event`, or a concurrent-mint mention across `findings.xml`, `rulings.xml` and the buffer returned only unrelated concurrency prose.
**The shape of the remedy, not the remedy itself.** Prevent at mint: make the id unique by construction at the writer, verify it against the loose events and the ledger after the write, and on a contested id renumber only the caller's own just-written file and retry — lock-free, no new artifact, and it closes the same-task overwrite as well. The obvious cheaper form, an exclusive create of `<id>-<task>-<kind>.xml` retrying on `EEXIST`, closes only the same-task class, because the id is not the filename; a cross-task duplicate needs the post-write uniqueness check. Diagnosis must accompany it: `recover` reports the duplicate as a fold blocker and `fold` names it, so a collided stream is never mislabelled. A **repair path is refused** — it would overturn `recover`'s "never rewrites recorded events; never deletes orphans" and `D41` at once.
**The repair that followed is governed by [D41](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md), not by this finding.** The maintainer ruled the hand-renumbering ungoverned and forbidden, permitted once as an escape from a deadlock the product created, and explicitly not a precedent until the PILOT decision. Read `D41` before citing this entry: the defect recorded here is the collision, not a licence to repair one.
Owner: a cursor-integrity bundle — `src/grace-cursor.ts` (`LINKS: M-CURSOR`) and its guards. Stays staged.

Finding.Title: ### F270 — no shipped verb prints a verdict's per-criterion `Result`/`Exit` tally; `gate verdict` records them and `review` only reports an unevaluated criterion, so row 19's "read them from the ledger" is readable only by opening the ledger. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `da727d0`.** `grep -n defineGraceCommand src/*.ts src/**/*.ts` lists every live root and sub-root — `apply, context, cursor, doctor, file, gate, graph, lint, module, plan, review, scaffold, spec, status, supersede, verification`; `gate`'s subcommands are exactly `approve, apply, archive, verdict` (`src/gates/command.ts:470`), and no verb is named for a verdict's criteria. `gate verdict`'s human output prints only `outcome`, `scope`, `classification`, `reason` (`src/gates/command.ts:439`–`446`) and its `--format json` payload is `stored`, which carries `findings`, `acks`, `snapshotDigest` and no criterion children (`src/gates/ledger.ts:400`–`447`); the criterion nodes are appended to the ledger element after `stored` is fixed (`src/gates/ledger.ts` `section.children.push({ tag: "Verdict", children: [...findingChildren, ...ackChildren, ...closeChildren] })`). `collectCloseEvidenceEvaluations` (`src/artifact/grammar.ts:2174`), the only reader of `AC-*` → `Exit`/`Result`, is called once, by `auditCloseEvidenceUnevaluated` (`src/review/core.ts:1874`), and only to test *presence* — it emits `review.close-evidence-unevaluated` for a criterion with no recorded evaluation and never prints the recorded `Exit`/`Result`. Row 19's remedy, "read them from the ledger, never from a hand-rolled reader", therefore names a read no verb performs.
**Proposed owner.** A `src/` bundle adding a `gate verdict --show` / `ngrace status` surface that prints each `Verdict`'s `AC-*` children with `Exit` and `Result`. Not paid by a teaching increment: no skill sentence can print what the engine does not emit, and the ledger element shape (`Verdict` → `AC-*` children with `Exit` and `Result`) is a `src/` contract.
Owner: a `src/` bundle (a verdict-inspection surface); stays staged here.

Finding.Title: ### F291 — the two artifact families the authority verifies most, change bundles and the record, are the only ones with no query verb; every close-time question is answered by a bespoke script. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `0545433`.** `bun run ngrace --help` lists sixteen commands, three of which are semantic query surfaces: `file` ("Query file-local neo-grace markup and private implementation context"), `module` ("Query shared neo-grace module artifacts") and `verification` ("Query neo-grace verification entries, scenarios, evidence requirements, and failure localization"). **No verb queries a change bundle (`spec.xml`, `plan.xml`) or the record** (`findings.xml`, `rulings.xml`, `registry.xml`, `decisions.xml` and their retired siblings). `src/query/command.ts` is not a counter-example: its header reads `PURPOSE: Citty CLI argument-form guard and error-channel routing`, `LINKS: M-CLI-INFRA` — it is the command-definition helper, not a query engine.
**The asymmetry is the finding.** The authority's entire function is verifying bundles and the record, and those are precisely the two families the CLI does not serve. Every question the close asks — what does this bundle pay; which `AC-*` carry `CloseEvidence`; what is in `ObservedWriteScope`; does this index `Entry` have its genre element; is this finding retired and by whom; what did the last `Verdict` record per criterion — is answered today by a `bun -e` script written fresh at the moment of asking, unauditable and not re-drivable by the next reader.
**The measured cost of that.** [F290](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) records two structural mis-readings in one session, both from hand-written patterns over XML: a `MustExist` regex that read **0** needles where `xmllint --xpath` read **13**, and an absence claim about a renderer that existed. The tools to be right were installed throughout; what was missing was a sanctioned, repeatable way to ask.
**It folds with an already-staged finding.** `F270` records that no shipped verb prints a `Verdict`'s per-criterion `Exit`/`Result` tally — the ledger stores it and nothing surfaces it, so every close reads the tally with a hand-rolled walk. That is this same gap in this same family. The two belong in one bundle: **a read-only inspection surface for governed artifacts.**
**Two properties the remedy must carry, both bought with this session's evidence.** (1) **Read-only.** It creates no state, so it cannot produce the class `F288` and the archived-bundle traps just cost four supersedes — a state the product can enter and no verb can leave. (2) **The engine's own parser**, so a query can never disagree with a gate; a second reader of the same bytes is a second source of truth, which is the defect `F289` produced inside one verb.
**What this does not fix, stated so the remedy is not oversold.** The defect behind `F290` was discipline, not capability. A verb makes the correct reading easy and auditable; it does not make the incorrect one impossible. `F290`'s teaching rule is the cheaper half and must land regardless.
Owner: an inspection-surface bundle, sequenced **after** [F288](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) — cursor integrity can still deadlock the repository, and a convenience does not outrank it. Carries `F270` and this entry together. Stays staged.

Finding.Title: ### F283 — a cursor `fail` attempt recorded *after* the fix that greens it is uncorroborated: `review.attempt-pair-identical-tree` reddens because both snapshots share the fixed tree, so a correction whose red already passed must be a **pass-only** attempt (or the fail written before the edit). **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 while executing `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016` at `0b0eba5`.** Two corrections to already-passed tasks (T-002 and T-003) — `MODULE_MAP` entries for three new `src/gates/ledger.ts` exports (`__predecessorMapView`, `__predecessorMemoStats`, `__resetPredecessorCache`) and two new `scripts/test-affected.ts` exports (`AFFECTED_EDGES`, `allTestFiles`), surfaced by `ngrace lint --path . --assertions current --change C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016` (2 errors, `markup.module-map-mismatch`) — were recorded as `fail` (signature kind `fix`) then `pass` **after** the `MODULE_MAP` header edit had already landed. `ngrace review --path . --change C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016` then emitted `review.attempt-pair-identical-tree` for both pairs (events 34→36 and 35→37): "no authored path outside `.ngrace/` differs across the pair … Red-first is not corroborated by any non-ledger content change (F9.10)". The audit is correct; the record is not — the `fail` snapshot was taken with the fix already in the tree.
**The honest forms.** (a) Record the `fail` in its own tool round trip *before* the edit, as the primary pairs did. (b) When the red has already passed — here the red was `lint`'s exit 1, captured in a round trip *before* the edit — record a single `ngrace cursor attempt --outcome pass` and disclose the pass-only correction in the report (`ngrace-execute` rule 13). A `fail` written after the fix cannot corroborate red-first and must not be recorded; `WriteEvidence` digests `ObservedWriteScope` at attempt-command time, so the ordering is the evidence.
Owner: a teaching increment (the cursor/attempt ordering for corrections). The two uncorroborated pairs are permanent in this bundle's run stream and cannot be removed; the authority's close sees them as two `review.attempt-pair-identical-tree` warnings.

Finding.Title: ### F285 — a plan's `ObservedWriteScope` must declare every file the **close** writes, not only the files its tasks write: when a spec assigns an act to the authority, the scope audit still charges that act to the plan. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `68ec888`,** driving the close of `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016`. The approved spec assigns the payment to the authority — "the approval write, the gates, the applied close and the flush are the authority's" — and excludes `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH` from `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC`, so the record writes are authorised. The approved plan's `ObservedWriteScope` names 25 files and **no record file**, because this bundle, unlike its predecessor `C-CLONE-FAITHFUL-TESTS-1-D68520A2`, has no payment task. The authority's `--flush` then wrote `findings.xml`, `decisions.xml` and `registry.xml`, and `ngrace review` returned three `review.scope-outside-write-scope` **errors**, one per record file, each reading "Changed file … is outside the declared write scope".
**No ordering avoids it.** The flush refuses once the bundle is archived (`flush-row-not-active` checks `.ngrace/changes/active/<change>`), and `--retire` requires the row to exist before it can move it, so the flush must run while the bundle is active — which is exactly the window the scope audit watches. `--retire`'s own post-archive record writes do *not* trip the audit, which is why the predecessor's close was clean and this one is not. Only a declaration in the plan would have prevented it.
**The generalisable rule.** Both prior scope findings — [F136](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) and [F282](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) — are about a *spec* omitting a file its deliverable forces. This is the same failure one layer down and one actor over: the *plan* omitting a file the *authority* is told to write. The check that catches it is to read the spec for every act it assigns to the authority, and confirm each such act's write targets appear in the plan's `ObservedWriteScope` before the plan is approved. The authority's approval of this plan applied neither that check nor `F282`'s.
**Cost, recorded because it is the argument for the check.** The maintainer ruled the remedy as a bundle supersede. `ngrace supersede` is bundle-level — there is no artifact-level plan repair — so the governance of a bundle whose execution was complete is discarded: 41 cursor events across two epochs, every red-first pair and `WriteEvidence` digest, stay in the superseded bundle's ledger, and the successor must re-record its cycles as pass-only against a tree where the work already stands ([ngrace-execute](skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md) rule 13). A missing line in a scope list cost a whole bundle's governance.
Owner: a teaching increment (the approval-time check), and the successor of `C-TEST-TIME-BUDGET-2-3EC1F016`, whose plan declares the record files.

Finding.Title: ### F290 — structural claims about an XML artifact were verified with regex, and regex read the structure wrong twice in one session; the parser and XPath were available throughout. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-17 at `0545433`,** by the authority, against its own verification of `C-RECORD-DECISION-FLUSH-1-368E01F2`. A hand-written pattern `<MustExist><Value>([^<]+)</Value></MustExist>` returned **0** baseline needles; `xmllint --xpath 'count(//BaselineAssertions/MustExist)'` on the same file returned **13**. The artifact writes each element across three lines, and the pattern assumed one. The consequence was not cosmetic: the authority briefly held that a plan declared no baseline needles at all, moments before approving it.
**The same disease in source, the same session.** A search for a decision renderer used `grep -n "renderLiveFinding\|renderLiveDecision\|function renderLive"`, found nothing, and the resulting brief asserted that no such renderer existed. `renderDecision` sits at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:437`. The pattern demanded the token `renderLive`, which the target never carried — [F138](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md)'s rule ("the pattern must be wider than the claim") applied to a function name rather than to a constant.
**Why the tools were already there.** `xmllint` is installed (`which xmllint` exits 0) and answers structure exactly: `count(//ObservedWriteScope/File)` → 9, `count(//ImplementationPlan/*)` → 5, `//BaselineAssertions/MustPassCommand/Command/text()` → the five commands. The repository ships its own parser, `parseGraceXmlArtifact`, which the authority already uses for every record claim — genre, layer, `PaidBy`, root arithmetic. The inconsistency is the finding: the parser for the record, regex for bundle artifacts, and both misses landed on the regex side.
**The rule, and it is not new.** `ngrace-spec`'s `acceptance_criteria_anchors` already says structural counts come from the shipped parser and never `grep -c`, and to prefer parsing the artifact when the claim is about structure. That passage binds the *executor authoring a spec*.
