Nothing binds the *authority verifying one*, and the authority is the party whose whole function is to distrust reports — so it is the party for whom a wrong structural reading is most expensive.
**Remedy.** State the rule where the verifying party reads it: a structural claim about an XML artifact — a count, a presence, an attribute value, which section holds a node — is answered by `xmllint --xpath` or by the shipped parser. `grep` locates; it does not testify.
**Amended 2026-09-18: the rule is not "use XPath", because XPath alone did not save it.** Four misses now share one cause, and the tool was different each time: `grep "renderLive"` for a function named `renderDecision`; a single-line regex for elements written across three lines; `grep … | head -5` reporting 4 call sites where there were 8; and `xmllint --xpath '//DurableScope/M-CURSOR'` returning 0 for an anchor nested at `DurableScope/GraphAnchors/M-CURSOR`. The last used the right tool and still failed. The common act is writing a pattern from an **assumed** shape. The rule that covers all four: **read the shape first — print the element, list the call sites, look at the nesting — and only then write the query.** A count is trustworthy only when the thing counted has been seen once.
Owner: a teaching increment (the reviewer/authority surface). Stays staged.

Finding.Title: ### F293 — a spec declared `Pays F288` while its own byte-invariance criterion forbade the write that pays it, and the payer-map repair sat outside the declared scope; the approval check reads the files a spec *names* and never asks what the *close* must write. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-18 at `baeadc2`,** by the authority, after approving `C-CURSOR-EVENT-ID-INTEGRITY-1-A0E753F3`. The spec states `Pays` **`F288`** and, in the same artifact, *"No record file is written by this bundle: `F288`'s retirement is a **later** flush between dispatches … and `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH` is deliberately left **out** of the `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC` excludes so an unexpected record write reddens."* `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC` is `git diff --exit-code b6d7aba -- . ':(exclude)src/grace-cursor.ts' ':(exclude)src/grace-cursor.test.ts' ':(exclude)README.md' ':(exclude).ngrace/changes'`, evaluated in the applied-archive state.
**The two branches, both measured, neither available.** Flushing at the close — while the bundle is active, as every bundle this session has done — leaves the record differing from the base when the criterion runs, and the record is deliberately unexcluded, so the criterion reddens. Flushing later is refused by construction: `--flush --change C-ARCHIVED-PROBE-1-00000000` returns `flush-row-not-active: … is not an active bundle` at exit 1, while the identical command against an active bundle exits 0 and mints the row — a discriminating probe, driven both directions on a throwaway. Once archived, a bundle can never mint its own row, so `F288` can never be paid by it.
**The compounding half.** `derivePayerMap` mints a token for every registry row whose name is an archive directory, and the walk asserts `derived.get(token) === baseline[token] ?? bundleMinted[token]` for **every** minted token (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2222`). `F288` is in neither map. The file holding `bundleMinted` is in neither the spec's write scope nor `AC-NO-OTHER-SRC`'s excludes, so the repair is unreachable from the approved boundary — the same shape as the payment itself.
**The fifth instance of one class, and the second after its own finding was written.** [F136](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) — a spec forcing a file whose module was missing from a list. [F282](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) — a spec removing a value whose guards it never scoped. [F285](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) — a plan omitting files the **authority** writes at the close. [F286](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) — an audit not conditioned on abandoned governance. Now this: a **criterion that forbids the write the spec's own `Pays` line requires**. `F285` was written by the authority and the authority then approved this spec without applying it.
**What the existing check misses, stated as the remedy.** The standing approval check reads each file the spec's `Constraints` *name* and confirms its module anchor — it is a check on the **enumerated set**. Nothing asks the prior question: **what must the close write, and does every criterion permit it?** The close writes the flush's four record documents, `--retire`'s three retired siblings, and the bundle's archive arrival; each must appear in the write scope **and** survive every byte-invariance pathspec. That is mechanical — the write set is derivable from `Pays` being non-empty — and it is the check whose absence has now cost five bundles.
Owner: the successor of `C-CURSOR-EVENT-ID-INTEGRITY-1-A0E753F3`, which excludes the record and scopes the payer-map file; and a teaching increment for the approval-time check, which belongs beside [F285](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md)'s.

Finding.Title: ### F296 — `ngrace-execute`'s "batch the fix, not the guards" has no rule for an indivisible mechanism whose guards can only green together, so the only red-first path is the retrospective red [F283](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml) forbids. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-18, from `C-CURSOR-EVENT-ID-INTEGRITY-2-E18DFE92`** (merged in PR #108, `c83dfae`). Two of that bundle's tasks landed their mechanism before their guards, so five verification cycles have no recordable red and `ngrace review` reports five `attempt-pair-unpaired-pass` infos. The executor refused to stage a retrospective red — correctly, because manufacturing one is precisely the act `F283` exists to name — and proved the guards non-vacuous by planted mutation instead. The skill passage that should have governed the choice says only "batch the fix, not the guards", which assumes the guards can be authored and driven red independently of one another. For a single lock-plus-renumber mechanism satisfying several `AC-*`, they cannot: every guard greens the moment the mechanism lands, and the only way to see red is to revert something already recorded.
**The maintainer's proposed remedy, quoted as given:** "Atomic Mechanism Exception: When a single indivisible mechanism satisfies multiple facets, authoring the minimal cluster of guards against the baseline to witness simultaneous red is permitted over sequential revert cycles."
**Three things it needs before it can ship as skill text.** (1) *Facets* is not a house term — the artifacts say acceptance criteria (`AC-*`), tasks and verification cycles. (2) It does not say **how the attempt pair is recorded**, which is the whole reason the gap exists: one `cursor attempt --outcome fail` for the cluster then one `--outcome pass` yields **one** pair for N guards, and whether the attempt-pair audit stays quiet for the other N−1 is a measurable question against `src/review/core.ts` that must be answered before the rule is written. (3) It must name the forbidden move explicitly — reverting a landed mechanism to manufacture a red — and say what happens when guards *were* authored late: the cycle is recorded pass-only, disclosed, and proven non-vacuous by planted mutation.
Owner: a teaching increment on `ngrace-execute`, gated on measuring the attempt-pair audit's behaviour for a one-pair/N-guard cluster. Stays staged.

Finding.Title: ### F298 — measured: one `fail`/`pass` attempt pair covers an N-guard atomic cluster, and `ngrace review`'s attempt-pair audit reports **one** pair without raising `attempt-pair-unpaired-pass` for the other N−1. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-18 executing `C-INSPECTION-SURFACE-1-2628AA2B` at `16538cd`,** answering the question [F296](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) is gated on — "whether the attempt-pair audit stays quiet for the other N−1".
T-001's mechanism (`parseVerdictNode` in `src/gates/ledger.ts` populating the `closeEvidence` field) is one indivisible change; its guard cluster is four cases in `src/gates/core.test.ts`, **three of which redded together** before the mechanism landed (the fourth is a vacuous-safe negative that guards against an over-eager fix, and greened pre-fix). One `ngrace cursor attempt --task T-001 --outcome fail` was recorded in its own tool round trip before the mechanism edit; one `--outcome pass` after. The whole bundle ran **six** such pairs (T-001…T-006).
`bun run ngrace review --path . --change C-INSPECTION-SURFACE-1-2628AA2B`, with the epoch open at execute, printed `Attempt-pair audit: ran over 6 fail→pass pair(s) … (0 finding(s))` — 6 pairs for 6 tasks and **0** findings: no `attempt-pair-unpaired-pass` and no `attempt-pair-identical-tree`. The audit is per-attempt, not per-test: it pairs a task's cursor `attempt` events and has no knowledge of test cases, so it stays quiet for the N−1 guards that have no pair of their own.
**Why this is the answer F296 needed.** The audit does not punish the atomic-cluster recording shape, so the Atomic Mechanism Exception can ship with its recording shape named: author the cluster against the baseline, witness simultaneous red in one round trip, record **one** `fail`, land the mechanism once, record **one** `pass`. The failure mode F296 feared — N fails against one pass leaving N−1 unpaired — does not occur if the cluster is recorded as one cycle, and it does occur if a `pass` is recorded without its `fail` (which is the audit's ordinary job).
Owner: [F296](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md)'s teaching increment, now unblocked.

Finding.Title: ### F302 — `TaughtIn` has a reader, a validator and a schema slot but no writer: `--flush --codify` stamps only `CodifiedIn`, so under the CLI-only-writes direction a decision taught in a skill cannot be annotated without a hand edit. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-18 at `220a061`,** by the authority, walking the close of the teaching increment before briefing it. The element is fully specified on the read side: `scripts/record-query.ts:162` reads it (`taughtIn: childTextOrNull(node, "TaughtIn")`), `taughtResolvesCheck` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:2000`–`2024`) refuses a missing `path`, an absent file and an absent `section`, and `scripts/record-serialize.ts:66`–`77` admits it in `childOrder` `^TitleBody(CodifiedIn|TaughtIn)*$` with attributes `path`, `section` (`:123`). On the write side: `flushRecord`'s only annotation branch is `opts.codify` (`:1661`–`1672`), which appends a `CodifiedIn kind=… ` child and nothing else; the `--flush` argv filter (`:2051`) knows `--codify` and no `--taught`; `grep -rn TaughtIn scripts src --include='*.ts' | grep -v test` returns the reader, the validator, the serializer and two comments — no write. The record holds **zero** `<TaughtIn` elements across all seven files (`grep -o '<TaughtIn'` returns nothing; the 7 `grep -c` hits are prose).
**The ruling it collides with, and the one it does not.** `C-TAUGHT-RULES`'s spec (Assumptions) records that "a resolving `TaughtIn` annotates and does not retire, teaching a rule in skill prose is not enforcement, and no shipped rule makes a `TaughtIn` owed by teaching" — so no bundle is *obliged* to stamp it, and this finding blocks nothing. But [D41](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md)'s own body names "a later teaching increment" in `ngrace-execute` as its teacher, and [D40](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) routes every governed XML change through the CLI; the annotation D41 anticipates is therefore unreachable by any permitted act. An element that can be validated and queried but never produced is the same shape as [F270](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md) (a tally recorded but never printed), one layer over.
**Remedy.** A `--taught D<n>:<path>:<section>` option on `--flush`, mirroring `--codify` (`flush-taught-absent` for a non-decision, and the existing `taughtResolvesCheck` run against the next-document before the write loop so an absent path or section refuses with all four files byte-identical). Multiplicity is already permitted by the schema (`*`), so no exists-refusal; a byte-identical duplicate is refused. Small enough to ride with the teaching increment, whose close is the first act that needs it — D41 taught in `ngrace-execute`.
Owner: the teaching increment (`F296 F298 F283 F285 F290 F293`), as a second deliverable under `scripts/`. Stays staged.

Finding.Title: ### F303 — `flushRecord` assembles buffer bodies into `String.replace` replacement strings, so an entry whose body contains a replacement-pattern sequence corrupts the next findings document and the flush refuses with a message that blames an unrelated index entry. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-18 at `03af506`,** first by the executor's plan-time close drive for `C-TEACHING-INCREMENT-1-B9D139EA`, then reproduced by the authority on a throwaway copy of the shipped tree, both directions. `--flush --change C-TEACHING-INCREMENT-1-B9D139EA` selecting the seven findings `F296 F298 F283 F285 F290 F293 F302` exits **1** with `flush-index-orphan: decisions.xml: Entry id="f1" token="F1" has no holding Finding/Decision in either layer of its pair`, and all four flush-written record files stay byte-identical; the identical invocation selecting the six without `F302` exits **0**, lands six `Finding` elements, and the validator exits 0.
**Cause.** [F302](docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.md)'s staged body quotes the serializer's `childOrder` regex, whose closing `$` is immediately followed by a backtick — the `$`` sequence that `String.prototype.replace` reads as "the portion of the string before the match". `flushRecord` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`) builds `nextFindings` (`:1653`), `nextIndex` (`:1654`), `nextRegistry` (`:1659`) and `nextRulings` (`:1660`) with `String.replace(closingTag, renderedEntries + closingTag)`, where the replacement string is assembled from buffer bodies; the `--codify` insertion (`:1671`) interpolates `kind` and `val` into a replacement string beside its `$1$2` capture references. Any body carrying `$``, `$&`, `$'`, `$$` or `$<digit>` is rewritten by the engine before it is written. The pre-write presence relation caught the corrupted next-document — a refusal, not a corrupted write — but its diagnosis names `F1`, the first entry displaced by the duplicated prefix, not the cause.
**Remedy.** A function replacement at all five sites (`replace(search, () => replacement)`, and at the insertion site a function taking the capture groups as arguments), with a test that flushes a body carrying the sequence beside a second finding and asserts both land once, the sequence written literally.
Owner: the successor of `C-TEACHING-INCREMENT-1-B9D139EA`, whose plan's close cannot land `F302` without it. Stays staged.

Finding.Title: ### F307 — `AC-UNIQUE-CONCURRENT` failed once in 25 CI runs on Windows, and the guard cannot say why: the concurrent-advance helper discards stderr, and the event write lock can be read empty between create and write, which makes a live holder look stale and sends the reader into an unguarded `unlinkSync`. **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-18 on PR #110 (`55bae41`), workflow run `35379364216`, job `windows-compatibility`:** `src/grace-cursor.test.ts:4119` — `expect(codes.every((code) => code === 0), "round 0 exits").toBe(true)` — received `false`; the test `cursor event-id integrity (C-CURSOR-EVENT-ID-INTEGRITY-2-E18DFE92) > concurrent advances with distinct tasks yield unique event ids (AC-UNIQUE-CONCURRENT)` failed at 2069 ms. The same job succeeded on `main` at `c83dfae` (the commit that introduced the test) and `220a061`, and in **24 of the last 25** runs of that workflow. The PR touches neither `src/grace-cursor.ts`, `src/grace-cursor.test.ts` nor `src/gates/ledger.ts` (`git diff --stat 220a061..55bae41` over those paths is empty).
**Why the log cannot diagnose it.** `runConcurrentAdvances` (`src/grace-cursor.test.ts:4044`–`4065`) spawns twelve `cursor advance` processes with `stderr: "pipe"` and resolves `proc.exited` only — the codes are asserted as a boolean `every`, so the failing process, its code and its message are all discarded. The first remedy is the guard's own: on any non-zero code, print each task's code and captured stderr before the assertion.
**The cause, measured 2026-09-18 on a throwaway copy at `55bae41`.** With `withEventWriteLock` instrumented to record every `stale` verdict, twenty runs of `AC-UNIQUE-CONCURRENT` (60 rounds, 720 contending processes) recorded **two** verdicts of `pid="" stamp=undefined alive=false` — the lock read **empty** — each followed by the unguarded `unlinkSync` of the live holder's lock; every run still exited 0 on macOS because the unlink succeeds there and the renumber masks the double-hold. The re-run of the same PR (`35379364216` attempt 2) failed the same test at round 2 after rounds 0 and 1 passed; Bun `1.3.14` and runner image `20260907.229.1` were identical across the two failing attempts and the green `main` run `35319134197`. Read from `withEventWriteLock` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:3317`–`3352`): The lock is taken with `writeFileSync(lockPath, "<pid>\n<stamp>\n", { flag: "wx" })` — create, then write, two steps. A concurrent contender that hits `EEXIST` then `readFileSync`s the lock can read it **empty**; `Number("")` is `0`, `processAlive(0)` is `false`, so `stale` is `true` and the contender runs `unlinkSync(lockPath)` — the live holder's lock — with no try around it (`:3337`–`3338`). On POSIX the unlink succeeds and two writers hold the section (the id renumber then masks it); on Windows, unlinking a file another process has open throws `EPERM`/`EBUSY`, uncaught, and that process exits non-zero — one of twelve, Windows only, rarely. The fix shape: write the lock to a temp name and `renameSync` it into place so it is never observable empty; treat a `NaN`/`0` pid as "unknown, retry", never as stale; wrap the stale-unlink in the same catch-and-continue the read already has.
Owner: a cursor-lock bundle, `src/` only, **immediately** — it blocks PR #110 through a required job. Stays staged.

Finding.Title: ### F308 — `cursor advance --open-epoch` without bounds allocates `w0:1-99` regardless of how many events earlier folded epochs already hold, so on any bundle with a folded history the next fold refuses `range hole at 1 for w0`, and `recover --fix` declines because the covering allocation is "present". **[verified]**
Finding.Body:
**Measured 2026-09-18** first by the executor on the production bundle `C-EVENT-LOCK-ATOMIC-1-9711E83D` (a T-001 correction after two folded epochs), then by the authority on a throwaway copy of the same bundle with four folded epochs and an empty `run/`: `ngrace cursor advance --change C-… --task T-003 --open-epoch` exits 0 and writes `23-T-003-opened.xml` with allocation `w0:1-99`; after a terminal, `ngrace cursor fold` exits **1** with `range hole at 1 for w0`; `ngrace cursor recover` reports `Valid covering allocation: present (w0:1-99)` and `Fold: blocked (range hole at 1 for w0)`; `ngrace cursor recover --fix` prints `Fix applied: no`. The only shipped remedy is a second `--open-epoch` with measured bounds (`--from 21 --to 200` on the copy; `--from 13 --to 200` on production), which supersedes the effective allocation last-writer-wins and lets the fold apply (`Events: 6`, exit 0). No hand edit of `run/` or `run-ledger.xml` was made in either case.
**Why it matters.** `ngrace-execute` rule 12 and the `opened` kind both say to open without `--from`/`--to` "unless you have a measured allocation need" — the ordinary instruction produces an unfoldable epoch on every bundle that has folded before, which is every bundle after its first end-state sequence (the final `--run-commands` opens a fresh epoch; a correction after that does too). The executor met it on the first correction this branch made. `D41` forbids the hand repair, so an agent that does not know the bounded-reopen trick is stuck at the fold.
**Remedy.** The unbounded open derives `from` from the next event id after the folded history (the ledger knows it), never a constant `1`; and `recover --fix` treats a covering allocation whose `from` precedes every loose event as the hole it is. Teaching: the bounded reopen as the interim recovery, in `ngrace-execute`'s `opened` kind.
Owner: a cursor-allocation `src/` bundle. Stays staged.
